Child A's two input roots are also authoritative over the historical co-located wording: load the
public/policy artifacts from one explicit caller-selected artifact root and the
`CoordinatorCredential` from a separate explicit credential path. The artifact loader must succeed
with `coordinator-auth.secret` absent and must never infer its path beside the backup.

The generic ingress rule is authoritative where the historical paragraph below is ambiguous:
`NONCE_REPLAYED` is an HTTP-200 response, so it advances sticky delivery to
`PossiblyDeliveredExact`. It stops only if an EARLIER endpoint attempt had already made this exact
request possibly delivered; a first replay advances and continues. HTTP 400 means no current signable
command was accepted/staged, not literally no node bookkeeping; a new logical retry uses a new nonce.

Everything below is preserved as decision history and frozen behavioral source for the two children,
but its “land in one task” instruction, combined 900/160 budget, claim/status, and ambiguous replay
wording are superseded and MUST NOT be implemented directly.

---

CODE CHILD 2 of btc-policy-mby. Build the shared operator trust boundary after M1 fixes the current artifact schema. Land the loader/client and signer in one rb-lite task to avoid speculative framework layers, while keeping coordinator credentials and spending authority structurally separate. This child targets the stage-1 co-located runtime; btc-policy-imb owns routable transport from stage 2 onward.

## Scope
- Add one syntax-tolerant `ParsedManifest`/artifact parser. A pre-mby manifest may parse for cold consumers but is NEVER hash-authenticated with a v0 layout and cannot become a live vault. Cold recovery authority is the descriptor plus consensus; no version-dispatched v0 preimage implementation.
- Convert only current protocol artifacts into a validated `LiveVault`: load/cross-check manifest.json, descriptor, manifest hash/current endorsements, sealed network (after btc-policy-5ag), node identities/endpoints, coordinator-auth secret/public key and wallet identity. Old version must fail before current-hash/current-field errors and before network access.
- Add a narrow stage-1 federation ingress client. Given one already-formed coordinator-authenticated request, try manifest-pinned loopback endpoints in deterministic order, always reusing the exact signed bytes and nonce. Maintain one sticky delivery disposition over a narrow typed transport result (connect-before-write versus ambiguous write/read; no error-string matching): `DefinitelyNotSent` becomes `PossiblyDeliveredExact` after an ambiguous write/read, HTTP 200 refusal, HTTP 408, HTTP 5xx/other unexpected status, or `Accepted`, and never moves backward. Some node-local refusals still stage/propagate while federation-uniform refusals do not, so the client must not encode an incomplete refusal taxonomy. HTTP 400 is explicit no-delivery for that endpoint (including transient body-read failure): preserve it, do not advance the sticky disposition for that attempt, and continue. HTTP 413 oversized input stops further direct delivery but cannot erase earlier possible delivery. A typed connect-time failure before any request byte was written likewise preserves `DefinitelyNotSent` and tries the next endpoint. Stop on `Accepted` and return its full structured payload (`commitment_id`, `first_seen`, `remaining_secs`) beside the disposition; M5 depends on that observable. `NONCE_REPLAYED` proves only nonce consumption, not which body consumed it: it stops delivery only when a prior endpoint attempt already made this exact request `PossiblyDeliveredExact`; otherwise preserve it and continue. At loop end, `PossiblyDeliveredExact` starts M4's conservative Core watch, while all-endpoint `DefinitelyNotSent` is immediately nonzero. No response or disposition is a quorum claim; only M4's Core observation decides command success. The client has no generic RPC escape hatch, user key, PIN-input method, signing method or `sendrawtransaction` capability. btc-policy-imb owns confidential authenticated coordinator-to-node transport after stage 1.
- Freeze the exact labelled signing seam decided in mby:

  ```rust
  pub enum UserAuthorization {
      Spend { wallet_id: WalletId, authorization: SpendAuthorization },
      Refresh { wallet_id: WalletId, authorization: RefreshAuthorization },
  }
  pub struct SpendAuthorization { spend: Psbt, escape: Psbt, escape_bumps: Vec<Psbt> }
  pub struct RefreshAuthorization { refresh: Psbt }
  pub trait UserSigner {
      fn authorize(&mut self, req: &UserAuthorization) -> Result<Signed, Error>;
  }
  ```

  `wallet_id` is only a display/lookup hint; sealed-state input membership remains authoritative. The Refresh arm ships now; no Refresh command.
- Add a software signer behind that seam using a user secret read only from an owner-only file, dedicated FD/stdin, or secret TTY path—never a literal argv value, log or artifact. Zeroize key material and verify its public key against the sealed descriptor before signing. It independently validates input membership from sealed state, derives policy/roles from PSBT scripts rather than trusting `wallet_id` or caller labels, uses SIGHASH_ALL, validates rung count/ceiling and truthful actual fees, and keeps PIN structurally absent.
- Require each PSBT to carry the full previous transaction for every input. Verify txid/vout/value/script and agreement with any witness UTXO before computing membership or fees; a caller-supplied witness UTXO alone is not authenticated prevout truth.
- Validate the authorization group, not just each PSBT: a normal Spend pair has the required shared input/primary relationship; an escape-class pair has exact nonempty disjoint input sets; all members share one sealed wallet/policy identity. Reject groups nodes cannot safely combine.
- Runtime authorization display shows exactly primary + base Escape when the sealed ceiling is zero and bumps are empty, including the actual base Escape fee. A valid distinct/disjoint all-escape pair remains signable after caller positions swap; render both as generic escape-destination transaction 1/2 with no authenticated immediate/residual claim. M2 owns reusable runtime display logic; M4/M5 invoke it.
- Reuse `policy-core`, existing HTTP and coordinator canonical request code. Do not extract the demo harness or invent generic wallet/client/display/fee trait hierarchies.

## Non-goals
Commands, Core inventory, composition/coin selection, base feerate selection, watch/broadcast, ladder construction, pending, recovery, hardware transport, encrypted keystore design, live use of pre-M1 manifests, routable transport, network selection, or user PIN UI. Hardware later replaces only the signer implementation.

## Red-first evidence
- Captured pre-mby artifacts parse, but live conversion fails specifically on version; tamper descriptor/hash/endorsement/coordinator secret/key/node identity independently and fail before network I/O.
- Exhaustively test only the ingress state machine here: all typed connect-before-write failures and HTTP 400s stay `DefinitelyNotSent` and continue; first-attempt `Accepted`, ambiguous write/read, 200 refusal, 408, 5xx and a representative unexpected non-5xx status transition to sticky `PossiblyDeliveredExact`; `Accepted` stops and preserves its full payload. HTTP 413 stops attempts without clearing prior sticky delivery. Cover pre-staging `COORD_NONCE_CAPACITY` followed by `Accepted`, node-local refusal followed by eligible peer `NONCE_REPLAYED`, and first-attempt replay continuing. Every endpoint attempt is byte-identical and one command draws exactly one 32-byte OS-CSPRNG nonce. Update SpendRequest/RefreshRequest documentation: a new logical retry re-signs with a fresh nonce, while same-command endpoint failover reuses the exact signed request. Core watch/broadcast composition remains M4's test scope; no response or replay is exact-body, quorum, or final-success proof.
- Wrong vault ID cannot authorize foreign inputs; caller mislabelling cannot turn Hot into Refresh; missing full prevtx or a present-but-false witness UTXO prevents membership/fee authorization.
- Empty ladder presents exactly two transactions and actual base fee; ceiling zero rejects a rung; a test-only nonzero ceiling rejects only above-ceiling rungs.
- Swap a valid all-escape pair and prove approval plus generic display. A mutation imposing positional role semantics must fail.
- Pair/group mismatches and mixed wallet/policy identities fail before signing.
- Structural tests prove client has no broadcast/signing key and UserAuthorization has no PIN. Named mutations cover artifact trust and authority separation.

## Likely files
New small `manifest.rs`/`sealed.rs`, `client.rs`, `signer.rs` modules (or equivalently narrow modules), `main.rs` declarations, small reuse in `http.rs`/`fed.rs`, policy-core/vault-proto types only where an existing public type must cross the seam, focused fixtures/docs.

## Hard rb-lite budget
**900 gross Rust lines maximum, additions plus deletions, every test line included: approximately 430 production + 470 tests.** Non-Rust: **160 gross lines**. Separate modules/types are required; a second abstraction hierarchy is forbidden. If full-prevtx and group-consistency proof cannot fit, split loader/client from signer rather than thinning trust-boundary tests or raising the cap.

title: Operator core A: sealed-artifact LiveVault and stage-1 federation ingress
description:
CODE CHILD A of tracking umbrella `btc-policy-mby-operator-core-signer-7vb`. Deliver only the
validated sealed-artifact `LiveVault` boundary and deterministic stage-1 federation ingress. This is
the loader/client half authorized by the original M2 budget valve after the combined rb-lite run
measured 899 gross Rust lines without implementing any signer. Child B owns every signing concern.
This child targets the stage-1 co-located coordinator; `btc-policy-imb` owns confidential authenticated
coordinator-to-node ingress and routable node-channel transport from stage 2 onward.

## Scope
- Add one syntax-tolerant `ParsedManifest`/artifact parser. A captured pre-M1 manifest may parse for
  cold consumers, but it is NEVER authenticated with an invented old preimage and cannot become a
  live vault. `LiveVault` conversion accepts only the current manifest revision (revision 2 at task
  creation). Reject an old version before current-only field/hash errors, sibling artifact or
  credential reads, or network I/O.
- Load the public/policy artifact set from one explicit caller-selected artifact root corresponding to
  the ceremony's `sealed/backup/` layout; the caller passes that artifact directory itself, so do not
  infer a ceremony root, append `sealed/backup`, or load node TOMLs. The artifact root need NOT contain
  `coordinator-auth.secret`, because the ceremony tells the operator to
  store that credential separately. Cross-check `manifest.json`, `descriptor.txt`, `wallet-id.txt`,
  `manifest-hash.txt`, current node endorsements/identities/endpoints, sealed network,
  descriptor/template, recovery timelock, wallet identity, and coordinator-auth PUBLIC key. Recompute
  the one current manifest hash; do not add version-dispatched preimages. Reuse existing
  template, descriptor-network, identity, endorsement, and manifest-hash validators rather than
  creating a second schema or trust hierarchy.
- Return a narrow policy/artifact `LiveVault` and load a separate concrete `CoordinatorCredential`
  from a second explicit caller-selected credential path. `LiveVault::load(artifact_root)` must not read
  or require the secret; `CoordinatorCredential::load(credential_path, &live_vault)` (or an equivalently
  narrow API) verifies the derived key against the manifest-pinned public key. Coordinator authority
  must not be embedded in the policy half that child B's signer consumes. Read the credential only from
  an owner-only regular file without following a symlink; keep textual bytes zeroizing and best-effort
  erase the parsed secret on Drop. Never infer the credential path by joining it to the artifact root,
  and ignore even a malformed decoy with that name beside the public artifacts. Use one concrete type,
  not a capability trait or generic keystore framework.
- Add one sequential stage-1 ingress client. Given ONE already-formed coordinator-authenticated
  `TaggedRequest`, serialize it once and offer the exact same signed body and nonce to manifest-pinned
  loopback endpoints in deterministic manifest order. Only the Host header may differ. The client
  owns no user key, PIN-input method, signing method, generic RPC escape hatch, or
  `sendrawtransaction`/broadcast path.
- Use a narrow typed transport result that distinguishes connect-before-write from ambiguous
  write/read; never branch on error strings. Maintain one sticky delivery disposition:
  `DefinitelyNotSent` becomes `PossiblyDeliveredExact` after an ambiguous write/read, any HTTP 200
  response (including a refusal or `NONCE_REPLAYED`), HTTP 408, HTTP 5xx, any other unexpected status,
  or `Accepted`, and never moves backward. Here `DefinitelyNotSent` means no signable command was
  accepted/staged; it does not claim that no authenticated bytes or nonce bookkeeping reached a node.
- A typed connect-before-write failure and an HTTP 400 whose status line was received — including a
  truncated body or subsequent body-read failure — preserve `DefinitelyNotSent` for that attempt and
  continue. Nodes can consume a coordinator nonce before a 400, but no signature/candidate/outbox/Hold
  survives those current paths; a NEW logical retry therefore uses a new nonce and signature. HTTP
  413 stops further direct delivery without erasing any earlier possible delivery.
- Stop on `Accepted` and return its complete structured payload (`commitment_id`, `first_seen`,
  `remaining_secs`). Preserve simple per-endpoint diagnostics (endpoint plus typed transport/status
  fact) for every non-accepted attempt, but never use diagnostic text for control flow and never retain
  secret bodies. `NONCE_REPLAYED` proves only nonce consumption, not which body consumed it: stop on it
  only when an EARLIER endpoint attempt already made this exact request possibly delivered; on a first
  replay, advance under the generic HTTP-200 rule and continue.
- No response or delivery disposition is quorum or final-success evidence. All-endpoint
  `DefinitelyNotSent` lets M4 exit nonzero; `PossiblyDeliveredExact` makes M4 conservatively watch
  Core. Only Core observation in M4/M5 decides command success.
- `LiveVault` MUST retain the canonical vault descriptor/template and user key, `CheckParams`
  membership/destination state, the 32-byte wallet identity, manifest/policy identity needed to bind
  one validated vault, the manifest-pinned coordinator-auth public key needed by the separate
  credential loader, and `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` for child B. It MUST contain no coordinator secret.
  Do not carry authenticated fields with no A or already-specified downstream consumer merely
  for completeness; M3 may add only the exact additional authenticated field it consumes.
- Update every SpendRequest/RefreshRequest nonce comment that says “per transmission”: same-command
  endpoint failover reuses one exact signed request and nonce; a new logical retry re-signs with a
  fresh 32-byte OS-CSPRNG nonce.

## Non-goals
`UserAuthorization`, `UserSigner`, software/user-secret signing, PSBT/full-prevtx validation,
transaction groups, ladder/fee validation, operator authorization display, commands, Core inventory,
composition/coin selection, base feerate selection, watch/broadcast, pending, recovery, hardware
transport, encrypted keystores, live use of old manifests, routable transport, concurrency, shutdown
machinery, network selection, or user PIN UI. No production command invokes this substrate until later
children, and closure must say so.

## Red-first and verification evidence

   version before any sibling read or network I/O. Do not synthesize the fixture from a current set.

   credential and prove the pair succeeds. Put a malformed/mismatched decoy named
   `coordinator-auth.secret` beside the artifacts and prove the explicitly selected external credential
   still succeeds, killing any mutation that reinstates `artifact_dir.join("coordinator-auth.secret")`.
   Independently tamper the selected secret and
   prove the pinned-public-key check fails. Prove the credential reader rejects a symlink, non-regular
   file, and group/other permission bits. Structural/Drop evidence must pin erasure and policy/credential
   type separation without exposing secret bytes in diagnostics or allowing B to acquire the credential.
4. Exhaustively table-test typed ingress transitions: connect-before-write and HTTP 400 with either a
   complete body or a post-status body-read/truncation failure continue without advancing; ambiguous
   write/read, HTTP 200 refusal, 408, 5xx, one unexpected non-5xx status,
   unparseable 200, and first replay advance sticky possible delivery; Accepted stops with all three
   payload fields; 413 stops and cannot erase an earlier possible delivery. Include pre-staging
   `COORD_NONCE_CAPACITY` then Accepted, node-local refusal then eligible peer replay, and first-attempt
   replay then Accepted. Prove each stop/continue count and every attempted body byte-identical.
5. Capture per-endpoint diagnostics for an all-down/refusing federation and prove endpoint/error facts

   decisions.
6. Use listeners retained through the assertion or an injected typed failure; do not reserve and drop

7. Prove exactly one already-formed command contains one 32-byte OS-CSPRNG nonce, all endpoint bodies
   reuse it, and a newly formed logical retry draws another. Mutation/structural checks must kill:
   old-version gate moved after sibling I/O, any one artifact cross-check bypass, body reserialization

8. Preserve all red/green and named mutation command/exit evidence from the first rb-lite run under an

title: Operator spend command: authorize, relay, and watch without broadcasting
description:
CODE CHILD 4 of btc-policy-mby. Expose the normal operator Spend command using M1-M3; this is the first product command and remains a relay, never a broadcaster.

## Exact command contract
`btc-vault spend` requires separate explicit `--artifacts <DIR>`,
`--coordinator-credential-file <PATH>`, `--user-key-file <PATH>`,
`--core-rpc-addr <IP:PORT>` (loopback only), `--core-cookie-file <PATH>`, destination address,
`--amount-sats`, `--request-ttl-secs`, and `--watch-grace-secs`. The artifact directory is the
non-secret runtime policy set and need not contain `coordinator-auth.secret`; no secret path has an
adjacent/default/environment fallback and no secret value appears in argv, environment, logs or CI
artifacts. User key and Core cookie use child A's no-follow, regular, owner-only, zeroizing file reader.
M3's one private RPC funnel re-reads and encodes the cookie into a `Zeroizing` buffer for EACH RPC and
drops it before returning, so no Core credential survives across the confirmation pause.

PIN input is exactly one stdin line of at most `vault_proto::MAX_PIN_BYTES`; stdin terminal echo is disabled
while it is a TTY, and noninteractive callers may redirect a pre-opened descriptor to stdin. Refactor the
existing nodekey echo guard into one direct, one-byte-at-a-time unbuffered fd reader with echo-on and
echo-off wrappers: operator confirmation uses echo-on, PIN and node preimage use echo-off, and every returned
buffer is zeroizing. At the exact cap, read one extra byte and accept only newline/EOF; cap+1 refuses rather
than authenticating a prefix. Do not use `StdinLock`/`BufReader` or otherwise prefetch PIN bytes outside the
zeroizing owner. M4 adds no PIN argv, environment, file, or separate FD-selection interface.
The user key uses M2's frozen file seam; genuine user-key FD support is outside M4.

TTL and watch grace must be positive and overflow-safe. Watch grace is an explicit deployment input at
least the maximum node combine slack plus one fixed `WATCH_POLL_SECS` interval, not inferred from
secret-bearing node configs. Nodes remain authority for hold/minimum/maximum age. HTTP responses are
unauthenticated: report only a decoded typed `RefusalCode` with the endpoint and a locally authored
explanation; never retain or print peer-controlled `check`/`detail`, which can reflect the plaintext PIN.
Application-owned secret buffers are zeroize-on-drop and rebuilt `SecretKey` temporaries are explicitly
erased, while child A's documented best-effort residual for copies inside cryptographic libraries remains.

Sequence: parse and retain only explicit paths/addresses, then load current secret-free artifacts. M3's
qhe-bounded Core calls open the cookie only for each snapshot/fee RPC. Compose primary + base Escape with
empty bumps; a composition refusal ends before user-key load, PIN, or ingress. Call `signer::describe`,
render every output+fee, capture the ordered `Vec<Txid>` for `[primary, escape, rung...]`, and require
explicit operator confirmation. Only then open the user-key file and invoke `UserSigner`. Consume `Signed`
and require BOTH its display to equal the approved preview byte-for-byte AND its ordered unsigned-transaction
txid vector to equal the pre-prompt vector; the display is the human check, while txids bind undisplayed
outpoints, version, locktime and sequences. Abort locally on either mismatch, then drop the signer so its
application-owned key bytes are erased before PIN collection.

After those equalities, strip every `non_witness_utxo` from the wire PSBT clones — M2 has already verified
them, SIGHASH_ALL/txids do not commit PSBT metadata, canonical `witness_utxo` remains, and nodes independently
fetch prevout truth. Retain the authenticated manifest `max_msg_bytes` in `LiveVault`. Before PIN, encode a
worst-case `MAX_PIN_BYTES` request shell with fixed-size nonce/signature placeholders and require BOTH its
raw `/sign` JSON and its exact channel-envelope expansion to fit the public node HTTP cap and sealed
`max_msg_bytes`; expose/reuse one narrow canonical size helper rather than duplicate the envelope. Recheck
the actual request before network. Oversize is a local typed refusal, never a 413 probe.

Then collect PIN and open/validate the coordinator credential. Sample wall time and `Instant` together ONCE,
derive both signed expiry=`wall_now + TTL` and watch deadline=`instant_now + TTL + watch_grace` with checked
arithmetic, and carry the monotonic deadline through ingress.
`CoordinatorCredential::with_seckey` scopes the rebuilt `SecretKey` to request authentication and erases it
before returning; replace the accessor that returns a `SecretKey`. Build/authenticate exactly one
`SpendRequest` with one fresh 32-byte OS-CSPRNG nonce and expiry derived from TTL, then drop the credential
before the first network byte. Do not construct this command around the long-lived demo coordinator.

Use child A's stage-1 ingress/failover contract rewired to qhe's bounded Ingress transport. Extend
`Outcome::Status(u16)` narrowly into `Outcome::Status { status, refusal: Option<RefusalCode> }` in endpoint
order. Never retain the peer-authored
`check` or `detail`; retained codes are reporting-only and cannot alter `Delivery`, while the existing
`NONCE_REPLAYED` branch remains the only refusal-specific state transition. M4 renders a local explanation
for `ExpiryTooShort` or `CommitmentExpired` without claiming one peer describes federation-wide settings.
Count this `ingress.rs` extension in M4's later budget; do not duplicate the endpoint loop.

HTTP responses are not cryptographically authenticated in v0. Once any request byte may have been written,
EVERY HTTP status — including 400 or stopping 413 — leaves `Delivery::PossiblyDeliveredExact`; a compromised
endpoint can propagate the exact request and lie in its response. Only exhaustion where every attempt is
`NotSent` before any write can return attributable no-delivery without watching. `Accepted`, eligible
`NONCE_REPLAYED`, refusal-only exhaustion, 400/413, and ambiguous transport prove at most possible delivery
and all start the same Core watch; none is exact-request/quorum/success evidence.

Watch through M3's existing typed `gettxout(primary_txid, 1, true)` only: vout 1 is M3's mandatory
vault-change output. Success requires a non-null result exactly matching the composed change value/script.
Use the monotonic deadline captured with signed expiry BEFORE ingress; never derive it from a later wall
read. Poll strictly sequentially at fixed `WATCH_POLL_SECS = 1`, with no jitter/backoff/concurrency, then
take exactly one final poll after the deadline. Each RPC retains qhe's own per-exchange bound.

Print this pinned warning immediately BEFORE the first network byte, repeat it before the first watch poll,
and repeat it on a null-result exit: delivery may already have happened; terminating ingress/watch is NOT
proof the transaction did not/will not broadcast; the change may already be spent; NEVER reissue without an
independent chain check. A valid Hot request's TTL
must outlive the node Hold+combine slack, so the foreground command normally runs at least the deployment's
Hold (24 hours by default); help/runbook tell the operator to keep that session alive and repeat the warning.

A null result is a conservative false negative, not command failure. Only positive Core observation is
success: nodes combined threshold partials and broadcast. No generic/unqualified lookup or new Core method
is added. Nodes combine/finalize/broadcast; the CLI never calls `sendrawtransaction`.

## Non-goals
Coin selection flags, arbitrary inputs, pending diff/journal, Refresh, recovery, incident escape-class command, ladder rungs, hardware transport, daemon/GUI, general monitoring, network-parameter work, or direct broadcast.

## Red-first evidence
- Current command routing returns nonzero before implementation.
- Fakes assert artifact/signer/coordinator authority separation; every explicit artifact/key/cookie/address
  argument and no fallback/environment credential; per-RPC cookie zeroizing with no ordinary auth/header
  copies; direct unbuffered confirmation/PIN reads, exact-cap newline/EOF, cap+1 refusal and TTY echo restore;
  authorize-before-PIN/coordinator ordering; exactly two displayed transactions/base fee; and exactly one
  32-byte OS-CSPRNG draw forming one signed request handed to A's ingress for byte-identical endpoint attempts.
- A recording seam pins
  `artifacts -> compose -> display -> confirm -> key load -> authorize -> display+txid equality ->
  signer drop -> PIN -> credential open -> request build -> credential drop -> first network byte`.
  Mutations opening either signing secret early, reaching network before credential drop, returning a
  `SecretKey` instead of scoping/erasing it, or substituting a same-display/different-outpoint request go red.
- Retained `RefusalCode`s preserve endpoint order, never allocate/retain peer `check`/`detail` PIN canaries,
  and cannot otherwise change endpoint ordering. Command-specific tests prove any post-write 400/413 is
  `PossiblyDeliveredExact` and enters watch (`compromised endpoint forwards -> lies 400/413 -> later Core
  broadcast`), while only all-`NotSent` exhaustion skips watch; node-local refusal followed by peer replay
  still broadcasts, and detached 408 later broadcast enters watch. M4 does not duplicate unrelated A matrix.
- Destination outside sealed Hot policy is refused by M3's final `policy_core::evaluate` before user-key
  load, PIN, or ingress; read-only loopback Core inventory/fee reads legitimately precede it. The signer
  independently re-runs the same authority.
- Full parents exist during M2 authorization but are absent from every wire PSBT; worst-case pre-PIN and
  actual request size checks cover HTTP and channel-envelope exact-cap/cap+1, and oversize reaches no PIN,
  credential, 413 probe or network. A mutation retaining full parents on wire goes red.
- An injected wall jump after the paired expiry/deadline sample cannot change the watch deadline;
  expiry-boundary broadcast is caught by
  exactly one final poll; acknowledgement without the output remains nonzero with the no-blind-reissue
  warning; interrupt-path recording proves the warning precedes network and is repeated at watch start;
  default-Hold
  help states the long foreground runtime; and node-side broadcast succeeds without direct `/sign`
  delivery to every node.
- Structural/recording boundary proves zero sendrawtransaction; mutation adding direct broadcast fails.
- Help/runbook make default-zero/no-rung behavior, command inputs, watch cadence/false-negative and
  no-blind-reissue rule explicit.

## Likely files
`main.rs`, a narrow `commands/spend.rs` or direct operator module, `sealed.rs` scoped credential/
`max_msg_bytes`, the shared nodekey direct secret-line helper, `ingress.rs` typed refusal-code retention,
the public canonical request-size/HTTP-cap seam, M3's Core watch seam, `docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md`, the
complete `docs/DESIGN.md` spend-flow sketch (Core composition, preview/binding, ordered ingress, node
broadcast, Core watch), and the exact operator-gap entries in `docs/THREAT-MODEL.md` and
`docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md`, plus CLI tests. Preserve unrelated unimplemented-command gaps.

## Budget must be re-derived before claim
The former 500-Rust mixed production+test cap is RETIRED under the owner production-only rule. M4 remains blocked on M3 and qhe; before M4 claim, re-read the landed seams and record a production-only Rust/non-Rust base, >=20% contingency, review allowance, reforecast, hard stop and mandatory split. Tests, helpers, fixtures, mutations and evidence are uncapped but every named sticky-delivery, expiry-boundary and no-direct-broadcast proof remains mandatory.

title: Refresh maturity monitoring: countdown, nags, and a safety-margin gate for funded vaults
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable spec review. Fable named this the single most likely cause of real loss of funds given the current specs, and NO BEAD OWNED IT -- verified by grepping all 46 beads for maturity/countdown/nag.

THE GAP. docs/DESIGN.md specifies refresh nags 'from day 120, shrill from day 150' and a ~90-day signing cadence. docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md requires Survivor vaults to 'publish their maturity countdown and Refresh before a mandatory safety margin'. btc-policy-mby delivers the refresh COMMAND, but its NON-GOALS line explicitly excludes 'monitoring/alerting integration' -- so nothing computes the countdown, nothing nags, and nothing blocks a stage from running past maturity. The specs require a control that no bead builds.

WHY IT IS THE TOP LOSS PATH, not merely a UX nicety. The 2-of-3 recovery keyset is distributed to THIRD PARTIES on purpose -- it doubles as the inheritance mechanism (CONTEXT.md). After the timelock matures it is a COMPLETE authorization path: no PIN, no user key, no Hold, no allowlist, no federation, no coordinator. Every other theft path in this design requires defeating something cryptographic or multi-party; this one requires only a calendar and two people (or one thief who has collected two key backups). The failure is INVISIBLE until the spend confirms, and the watchtower's recovery-path alert is POST-SPEND -- by the time it fires the coins are moving and the normal path is already dead.

It is worse today than the design assumes: a sealed vault cannot be refreshed at all (threat-model R9, btc-policy-mby), so ANY funded sealed vault is on a fixed fuse from its first deposit. And the relative timelock runs PER UTXO from each coin's confirmation, so there is no single vault-level maturity date -- a straggler deposit made after Lockdown starts its own clock.

DELIVER:
(1) A per-UTXO maturity computation -- earliest maturity across the vault's unspent set, not a vault-level constant, derived from each coin's confirmation height and the descriptor's timelock.
(2) A countdown surface an operator can read WITHOUT the coordinator being trusted or even alive, since a dead coordinator is exactly when a vault drifts. Prefer something derivable from the descriptor and a chain view alone.
(3) Nags at thresholds expressed as FRACTIONS OF THE VAULT'S OWN TIMELOCK -- 2/3 and 5/6 of it -- NOT as fixed day counts. On the 180-day default those land on day 120 and day 150, matching DESIGN.md, which is where the fixed numbers came from. THE FIXED NUMBERS ARE WRONG IN THIS GRAPH: btc-policy-wdu (same gate, P1) makes the timelock configurable per vault, so on a 90-day vault a day-120 nag fires AFTER maturity and a day-150 nag never fires at all -- the exact invisible-calendar failure this bead exists to prevent, on precisely the vaults wdu makes weakest. The 'mandatory safety margin' ROLLOUT-PLAN.md refers to but never numbers must likewise be a fraction, not a day count.
(4) A stage gate: a Survivor vault that crosses the safety margin during an observation run either gets refreshed or the run aborts. Today the stage-8 soak's whole purpose ('run it for a while') pushes in the opposite direction.
(5) State plainly what this does NOT do: it protects the operator who looks. It is not a control against a recovery-key holder who acts, and it must not be written up as one.

DEPENDS ON btc-policy-mby (the refresh command must exist before a nag can tell anyone to run it).

VERIFY: a regtest vault with mixed-age UTXOs reports the correct earliest maturity; nags fire at both thresholds ON THE DEFAULT TIMELOCK **AND** ON A SHORT NON-DEFAULT ONE (the second case is the real test -- an implementation with hardcoded day counts passes the first and fails the second, so a VERIFY that only exercised the default would rubber-stamp the bug); the safety-margin gate refuses to let a stage run continue past the margin; the countdown is correct for a coin deposited AFTER Lockdown (the straggler case, which is the one that has no remedy).

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY (bead-polish 2026-07-30): THE NOTIFICATION CHANNEL BELONGS TO btc-policy-2oz, NOT HERE. This bead owns COMPUTING maturity and deciding WHEN a nag is due; 2oz owns getting a message to a human and handling a dead delivery path. Filed separately, both described 'notify the operator', which would have produced two channels with two failure modes and two things to configure. A maturity nag is delivered through 2oz's channel.

title: Mutation-test the attack harness (DONE: red on an injected Lockdown fault, blind to an injected mixed-class one)
description:
FILED 2026-08-09 at the close of btc-policy-9yf, named independently by BOTH review models when asked adversarially what that bead's evidence does NOT establish.

9yf proved the launch gate reports a deliberately introduced regression. It proved it via `demo first-light`, which is gate step 9. `attack all` is step 12 and was SKIPPED, because the gate stops at the first failing step.

CORRECTED 2026-08-09 after codex review of the closure PR: the first version of this bead said
attack all "has never been shown to fail". THAT IS FALSE and contradicts records already in this
graph. btc-policy-rt0 documents escape-class-sequences failing deterministically (15/16) on main
across three consecutive runs, and btc-policy-6nq's closure note cites "attack 15/16" as its gate
result. The harness demonstrably reports failures.

SO THE POSITION TODAY IS NARROWER, AND STILL WORTH CLOSING: attack all has never been shown to
fail on a DELIBERATELY INTRODUCED fault. Every observed failure was spontaneous — and rt0's own
later notes attribute that one to load-sensitivity on a shared box, since CI passes the same
scenario. A spontaneous failure shows the harness is not vacuously green; it does not show the
harness is SENSITIVE TO A SPECIFIC SAFETY REGRESSION, which is what a negative control
establishes and what btc-policy-9yf demonstrated for the demos but not for attack all (the gate
stops at the first failing step, and 9yf's control failed at step 9, so step 12 never ran).

TWO DELIVERABLES:
(1) A negative control for the HARNESS. The constraint is ONLY about earlier steps of the
    launch-gate JOB, not about unit tests (corrected 2026-08-09 after codex review; the first
    version of this bead got it wrong). `check` and `launch-gate` are independent jobs with no
    `needs:` between them (.github/workflows/ci.yml), so a red `test` leg CANNOT stop
    `attack all` — only an earlier step inside launch-gate can, because steps within a job run
    in sequence and stop at the first failure. So: the fault must NOT be caught by
    demo first-light, theft-refused or recovery-drill (steps 9-11); it is FINE, and by the
    method note below actively desirable, for a unit test to catch it too. Require the named
    scenario's scorecard row to go red regardless of what other jobs do. Candidate: break the signer/partial COUPLING or the RELEASE-GATE so a
    scenario's safety assertion fails while first-light and theft-refused still pass. Confirm
    the specific scenario reports RED and names itself in the scorecard.
(2) A negative control for the OUTPUT-DERIVED CLASS CHECK (ADR-0013 section 3). During 9yf's
    control this check independently refused the spend after the allowlist was removed, which
    is what kept the demonstration honest ('a weakened control is detected', not 'funds
    leave'). But that means the class check is itself load-bearing and has never been
    falsified. Break it alone and confirm something goes red.

METHOD NOTE, learned from 9yf: the control must fail on BEHAVIOUR, not on a lint or a
compile error. Suppress the incidental warnings so the signal is the safety assertion. And
verify locally that the fault bites (a cheap unit-test run) BEFORE spending a ~47-minute CI
cycle, so the CI result is a confirmation rather than a discovery.

DO NOT close this by arguing the harness is well-tested, or that scenarios have failed in the
past for flaky/load reasons (see rt0). A gate nobody has watched fail on a KNOWN fault is not
known to be a gate — that sentence is 9yf's, and it applies here unchanged.

VERIFY: a recorded CI run where attack all reports RED for a deliberately introduced fault,
with the failing scenario named in the scorecard, plus the same for the class check; the
throwaway branches deleted afterward and the run URLs recorded here.

HOW TO REBUILD 9yf's REPRODUCER (recorded 2026-08-10, because the branch that held it was deleted).
The branch `test/9yf-negative-control` (tip 5a53e10c381dd321d2842016ff4eaa0c68db609c, on top of
66704b2) was deleted from the public repo on 2026-08-10: it removed a real custody control from
policy-core and sat unmarked in a public branch list. The EVIDENCE it produced is unaffected and is
what ADR-0017 cites — CI run 31238105663, which is a published run, not a branch.

The fault itself was two lines in `crates/policy-core/src/lib.rs`, at the top of
`check_destinations`, and is reproducible from this description alone:

    #[allow(unreachable_code, unused_variables)]
    fn check_destinations(psbt: &Psbt, params: &CheckParams) -> Result<(), Violation> {
        return Ok(());
        ... existing body ...

The `#[allow]` is part of the experiment, not sloppiness: without it the now-dead body trips
`-D warnings` and `check` goes red on a LINT, which would answer a different question than the one
being asked (does the gate catch a BEHAVIOURAL regression).

Two things that branch's own comment got WRONG, corrected here so a rebuild does not inherit them:
it called this "a real theft path", and it is not — the output-derived class check (ADR-0013 §3)
still refused the spend, which is exactly why deliverable (2) below exists. What the run showed is
that a weakened control is DETECTED, not that funds leave.

For THIS bead the same fault is not reusable anyway: it fails at step 9 (`demo first-light`), so
`attack all` at step 12 never runs — which is the entire reason this bead is open. Deliverable (1)
needs a fault that passes steps 9-11 and fails inside the harness.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
RESULTS, 2026-08-10. Both deliverables ran. They point in OPPOSITE directions and
neither may be quoted without the other.

METHOD, and it differs from 9yf's in a way that matters. 9yf ran its control in CI because its
claim was about the CI JOB. This bead's claim is about the HARNESS BINARY, so both controls ran
LOCALLY and neither fault ever left the working tree. No branch carrying a live safety regression
was pushed — a deliberate change of method after `test/9yf-negative-control` was deleted from the
public repo on 2026-08-10 for exactly that hazard. Read every result below as a property of the
binary. NONE of it is a CI run, and none of it says anything new about the launch-gate JOB.

Each run was taken one at a time on a shared box, because rt0 records this harness as
load-sensitive here and two concurrent federations would manufacture the very flake that would
make the results ambiguous.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
(1) HARNESS negative control — SATISFIED. The harness DOES report red on a
    deliberately introduced safety regression.

FAULT: crates/vault-node/src/channel.rs, ChannelState::lockdown_due —
    store.armed.active & (now >= store.armed.fire_at) & false
Lockdown at T never becomes due, so an ARMED node keeps accepting new signing forever. This breaks
the second half of the safety track ("freeze + UNCONDITIONAL Lockdown at T") and leaves the freeze,
the sweep and every refusal path untouched.

WHY THIS FAULT CLEARS STEPS 9-11, checked BEFORE injecting rather than discovered after: demo.rs
mentions lockdown ZERO times, so the demos cannot see it by construction. That was the constraint
9yf's fault failed.

MEASURED:
  clean    attack arm-split-closed  PASS  134s  1/1 held  exit 0
           (its row asserts "...yet all entered Lockdown at T")
  faulted  demo first-light         exit 0     step  9 survives
           demo theft-refused       exit 0     step 10 survives
           demo recovery-drill      exit 0     step 11 survives
           attack arm-split-closed  FAIL  178s  0/1 held  exit 1
             "node_id(s) [0, 1, 2] did not enter Lockdown at T; lockdown at T is
              unconditional (ADR-0012 invariant i)"
           plus per-node diagnostics naming each node's last committed decisions, so the report is
           attributable rather than a bare red.
           attack all               FAIL  ~41min  1/16 held  exit 1
             "ADVERSARIAL HARNESS FAILED - a duress safety assertion did not hold"

FULL-RUN EVIDENCE, added 2026-08-10 after codex review pointed out that this bead's VERIFY asks for
`attack all` and the first pass had only run ONE scenario. That objection was correct and the
single-scenario run did not satisfy it: `attack all` takes a full-run dispatch path a selected run
never reaches (`requested_full_run && !complete_scorecard`, crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs:244-249).
So it was run. 15 of 16 scenarios FAILED, each naming itself in the scorecard:

  FAIL arm-split-closed 180s        FAIL hold-expiry-race 153s
  FAIL censorship-residual-bounded 78s   FAIL lockout-then-duress 116s
  FAIL selective-delivery 149s      FAIL duress-resubmission 116s
  FAIL two-spend-probe 364s         FAIL reboot-death 193s
  FAIL toxic-parent 76s             FAIL fire-time-failure 79s
  FAIL in-flight-refresh 112s       PASS reorg-watchtower-cursor 40s
  FAIL escape-class-sequences 412s  FAIL reorg-duress-lockdown 79s
  FAIL reorg-escape-resettles 193s  FAIL recovery 147s

The SINGLE survivor is the result worth reading, not the 15: `reorg-watchtower-cursor` is the one
scenario that never calls `wait_for_lockdown`, so it is the one scenario that does not assert the
invariant this fault broke. The harness went red in exactly the places that assert the broken
property and stayed green in the one place that does not — the failures are ATTRIBUTABLE to the
injected invariant rather than a blanket collapse, which a fault that reddened all 16 could not have
shown.

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
(2) CLASS-CHECK negative control — SATISFIED as written ("break it alone and
    confirm something goes red"), and the thing that went red was NOT the harness.

FAULT: crates/policy-core/src/lib.rs, classify() — the (false, false) mixed-class arm returns
Ok(Classification { class: TxClass::Escape, hot_outflow: 0 }) instead of Err(PSBT_INCONSISTENT).

CORRECTED 2026-08-10 after codex review of PR #8. The FIRST attempt returned Hot, and calling that
"the documented duress bypass" was WRONG: Hot takes the Hold (crates/vault-node/src/lib.rs:5873),
the Hot budget and the duress freeze, so no extraction was possible and attack all's green run on
that fault was CORRECT rather than blind. The bypass classify's doc comment actually describes
(crates/policy-core/src/lib.rs:74-79) is misclassification as ESCAPE, which fires at `now`
(vault-node/src/lib.rs:5877) — so a mostly-to-hot + dust-to-escape spend completes IMMEDIATELY

Both deliverables ran 2026-08-10; method, numbers, limits and the VERIFY DISPOSITION are in the description, which is authoritative over this summary. The two halves point in opposite directions and must be quoted together.

(1) HARNESS IS SENSITIVE. The single survivor, reorg-watchtower-cursor, is the one scenario that never asserts Lockdown, so the reds are attributable to the injected invariant rather than a blanket collapse. That survivor also falsified a pre-existing claim in docs/TEST-PLAN.md that EACH scenario asserts the safety track; the exception is now named there.

(2) ITS SENSITIVITY IS UNEVEN. Corrected twice after review, so read this and not any shorter summary. The fault is classify's mixed arm returning ESCAPE (not Hot -- Hot takes the Hold and the freeze, so the first attempt opened nothing and its green harness run was CORRECT). Under ESCAPE: cargo test caught it (exit 101, 681 passed / 4 failed, including a differential oracle and a test asserting attacker-controlled outputs are only ever hot-or-refused); all three demos were BLIND, including demo theft-refused, the repo's named v0 acceptance artifact; and attack all held 16/16 exit 0. Filed as btc-policy-u98 (P1).

MAGNITUDE, bounded from both sides -- docs/adr/0017-one-external-review-at-stage-9.md owns the full statement and its citations. DEFEATED, all keyed on class == Hot: the Hold, the rolling-window reserve, the duress freeze; each spend is signed, combined and BROADCAST immediately rather than after the Hold ("settles" would overstate it, since confirmation still needs a block). NOT DEFEATED: the per-transaction Hot budget, which is class-independent and caps every spend at hot_max_per_tx -- MANDATORY operator config with NO default, so there is no "shipped" figure; and arming plus terminal Lockdown at T, which take no class. Arming is t-of-n CONFIRMATION-gated, not PIN-gated: fire_arm_hook records intent only, and confirm_carrier is the one write that arms. That makes the bound stronger, because completing the drain needs t signers and t signers is exactly the arming threshold -- the extraction arms the federation by construction. So: drain at the cap, repeatable for the duress-delay window, then terminal Lockdown. NOT "repeatable without limit". Two qualifications cut back: T MAY remain at its maximum (this spend leaves no hot Hold, but another pending one would still supply a smaller deadline), and THREAT-MODEL R11 says the delay before Lockdown has no finite bound, so composed with lock starvation the window is not bounded by configuration at all. And the extraction requires STOLEN HOT KEYS -- the destinations are the user's own hot wallet, so without them the outcome is a hot-wallet move at the cap, not attacker receipt.

LIMITS, do not upgrade: sensitivity to one injected fault in one invariant is not sensitivity in general, and (2) is the measured counterexample; only the MIXED arm of classify was falsified, NOT the unrecognized-output branch that refused 9yf's spend; CI as a whole DOES catch (2), because cargo test runs in the independent check matrix job, so this is not an open theft path in main; two of this bead's three VERIFY criteria are unmet AS WRITTEN -- (b) because attack all did not report red for the class fault and cannot until u98's scenario exists, and (c) the recorded-CI-run criterion, superseded by choice, whose cost is chiefly the loss of CI's retained artifacts. title: Resolve the node lifecycle contradiction (ADR decision; the drill is btc-policy-h22)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (codex #2). The operational documents are MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE, which means routine maintenance has no valid security-preserving procedure:
 - ADR-0005: the host is SEALED — SSH uninstalled, no administrative access path, 'no reset, no reconfiguration, no upgrade-in-place'.
 - ADR-0007: a rebooted node is a DEAD node (tmpfs; the reboot wipes key, Lockdown latch, generation marker).
 - docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md: each node starts once and its preimage is destroyed.
 - docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md: every start needs the preimage, and it is a backup item.
(The rolling-restart claim in UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY was already deleted in 14c2312 as unperformable under ADR-0005; this bead resolves the REMAINING tension rather than papering it.)

DECIDE, in an ADR, ONE model:
 (a) immutable one-shot nodes — every binary or config change is a vault migration, the preimage is genuinely destroyed after first start, and there is no supported restart; or
 (b) recoverable hardware-backed nodes — the signing key lives in hardware rather than being re-derived from an operator preimage, restart is a supported operation, and Lockdown becomes a DURABLE MONOTONIC latch rather than something a reboot clears.
Option (b) is the one codex recommends longer-term; option (a) is what the code implements today. Whichever is chosen, the ADR must supersede or amend the losers explicitly — this failure mode is documents disagreeing, so a new document that merely adds a fourth voice makes it worse.

SPLIT 2026-07-30 (bead-polish): THE DRILL MOVED TO ITS OWN BEAD (see below). This bead is now the DECISION ONLY, which is what btc-policy-qbt (stage 5) and btc-policy-juq are actually gated on. The decision needs stage-4 attrition data (btc-policy-s12) and nothing else; bundling the drill with it made stage 5 wait on migration tooling it does not need.

VERIFY (decision): an ADR exists choosing (a) or (b); it EXPLICITLY supersedes or amends every losing document rather than adding a fourth voice -- this failure mode is documents disagreeing, so a new document that merely joins the argument makes it worse; and every operational doc is updated to match. The destructive drill that proves the chosen model is survivable is a separate bead and gates the same downstream work.

title: 9y5.7 follow-up: batch the escape-ladder mempool residency scan
description: codex 9y5.7 pass-2 [P2]. mempool_escape_rung (crates/vault-node/src/lib.rs ~3091) loops over every ladder rung calling backend.mempool_transaction(txid), and BitcoindBackend::mempool_transaction (chain.rs:1184) issues a FULL getrawmempool (mempool_txids, chain.rs:688, uncached) on every call. title: Sealed node image: ADR-0005 build (no SSH, no admin path, tmpfs, reboot-death)
description:
FILED 2026-07-29 from the plan review (Fable Q6.3). Rollout stages 4,5,7,8,9 all require SEALED HOSTS, and the plan and bead s12 both cited btc-policy-4y3 as 'the sealed-host build' — but 4y3 is COORDINATOR host hardening: a different machine, a different threat (THREAT-MODEL R8b). The ADR-0005 sealed NODE image had NO BEAD AT ALL; the s12 -> 4y3 edge worked only by title confusion.

DELIVER the reproducible sealed node image ADR-0005 actually specifies: SSH uninstalled, no administrative access path of any kind, no reset, no reconfiguration, no upgrade-in-place; config and key material on tmpfs so a reboot wipes the signing key, the Lockdown latch, and the process-generation xattr (ADR-0007); the node's only surfaces being its API (/sign, /channel, /events, /healthz, /pending) and its chain backend. The image build must be reproducible and documented — an operator has to be able to rebuild and diff it, since after sealing there is no way to inspect the running host.

CARE: the seal is what makes duress Lockdown irreversible BY ANYONE, including the legitimate owner — that is why coercion has no reset to demand. Any capability left on the host that could restart or reconfigure a node is the reset a wrench attacker asks for. Enumerate explicitly what survives on the host and why a coercer cannot use it.

CONSEQUENCE TO STATE PLAINLY IN THE ARTIFACT: with this image, patching a node costs a full vault rotation and a dead node has no remedy. Stages 4 and 7 exist to measure whether that is livable (bead s12).

VERIFY: two independent builds of the image produce identical artifacts; a sealed node serves the Path suite; and a written enumeration of residual host capability, reviewable by an external auditor.

title: Record channel-mode Carrier deadlines in nonce liveness and capacity
description:
Code child of btc-policy-5io. Implement only acceptance-fixed `D` in channel-mode coordinator-nonce liveness/capacity. Depends on closed q6v. No Carrier intent/memo retirement or receipt behavior in this run.

## Scope
- When `Node.channel` is present and a Spend nonce is atomically accepted, sample that channel's production-fixed/test-pinnable `HotClock`, compute checked `D = M + (E - W)`, and retain immutable `D` in the nonce entry. Absent-channel Spend and Refresh remain wall-only.
- Nonce replay, `live_entries`, capacity, pruning and high-water advance use `wall_now < E || mono_now < D` for channel-mode Spend. A different body cannot reuse the nonce until both end. No release transition, second clock, new cap/schema/config/lease.
- Thread the accepted deadline toward the later Carrier claim without weakening q6v's acceptance-to-claim ordering. Include `D` unmasked in `SignStateShape`; pin monotonic test time to a value distinct from wall `now` and correct its stale “needs no clock pin” comment.

## Evidence
Observe red first for wall-expired-but-monotonic-live replay/capacity and rollback reuse. Green covers `<D`, `==D`, `>D`; wall-live/mono-dead and wall-dead/mono-live; absent channel; Refresh; full capacity no consume/relay; high-water only through actually removed expiries; exact shape symmetry. Named mutations independently remove monotonic OR-liveness, make absent-channel allocate D, or couple pinned monotonic to wall time.

## Hard rb-lite budget
**650 gross Rust lines maximum, every test line included: ~230 production + 420 tests.** Gross is additions plus deletions against the task base. Evidence/docs outside the Rust cap: 24 rendered lines. Stop and re-split rather than compress tests.

title: docs/DESIGN.md audit: it still schedules the shipped harness as future work and describes a weaker CI
description:
FILED 2026-08-08 by PR #6's consistency pass; RESCOPED 2026-08-09 from a site list to a FILE
AUDIT, because three successive review passes each found sites the previous enumeration missed.

THE PROBLEM: docs/DESIGN.md still describes the adversarial harness as unbuilt future work and
states acceptance criteria in terms of a scenario set that docs/TEST-PLAN.md:8/:48 formally
retired. The shipped reality is 16 scenarios in crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs (SCENARIO_NAMES),
wrapped by crates/vault-cli/tests/e2e.rs, SCHEDULED on every push (first failure skips the rest — never 'always runs') as the largest step of the
launch-gate job. TEST-PLAN and the code are the correct side; DESIGN.md predates the gate.

KNOWN SITES — examples, NOT the closure checklist. Do not treat this list as complete; it grew
from 2 to 5 to 8 across three review passes, which is why this bead is now an audit:
  :36   "Later (`btc-vault attack [all|<scenario>]`)" — that command exists and is SCHEDULED
        on every push, in the qualified sense this bead's header states: it is step 12, and
        the GATE steps (through `attack all`) carry no `if: always()`, so a failure in
        steps 9-11 skips it. Scope that to the gate steps, not to the job: the scorecard
        (ci.yml:289) and the artifact upload (ci.yml:367) DO carry `if: always()`, on
        purpose, because a failed gate's artifacts are the ones worth having. Do NOT write
        "runs
        on every push" — that is the unconditional guarantee `docs/TEST-PLAN.md` retracts.
        Only the "on the user's own VPSes" clause is still future.
  :60   a third variant of the retired scenario list.
  :77   a SEVEN-item ancestor of the retired list, inside the historical Approach A/B/C options
        analysis (archival — needs a supersession tag, not deletion).
  :102  workspace-shape table: "vault-cli/  # coordinator + demo runner (later: SSH deployer +
        attack scenarios)". Worst of the set: a layout table is what a new reader takes as
        ground truth.
  :124  "**v1** — Approach B: deployer, sealing ..., attack scenarios."
  :329  the v1 success criterion stated over the retired set, including an honest-failure case
        (`compromised-quorum: succeeds`) that is not among the 16 shipped names.
  :336  "CI: GitHub Actions — test + clippy on PR" — names two of five jobs and scopes them to
        PRs. ci.yml triggers on push/pull_request/workflow_dispatch, the check matrix has four
        legs, and launch-gate is a second job. TEST-PLAN:67 says the opposite, and quotes verbatim: it calls the job
        "**scheduled on every push**" and then '"Scheduled", not "all four always execute":
        the gate steps deliberately carry no `if: always()`, so the first one to fail skips the
        rest'. Do NOT restore an unconditional-execution guarantee when fixing :336.
  :344  Next Steps step 3 prescribes BUILDING the retired nine-scenario playbook engine.
  :46   "and demos it — the `compromised-quorum` scenario succeeds on purpose" — present tense,
        a claim about what ships; that name is not among the 16.
  :345  "demo GIF of both acts (refusal + hold-clawback)" — NOT A DEFECT, listed here so the audit
        does not "fix" it. That line describes the still-shipped `demo theft-refused` act two
        (the attacker's allowlisted spend clawed back by an instant escape sweep, demo.rs), which
        is live behaviour. Only `hold-clawback` AS AN ATTACK-SCENARIO IDENTIFIER is retired.
        Leave this line alone.
  :341  A DIFFERENT defect class, included because it is in the same file and the same sweep
        will surface it: "Test plan artifact:
        ~/.gstack/projects/btc-policy/user-unknown-eng-review-test-plan-20260713.md" points at a
        path that does not exist. The artifact is in-repo at docs/TEST-PLAN.md, same generator
        and date, and ADR-0013 cites it by name. Fix the pointer; do not delete the line.

TWO KINDS, and they need different fixes: archival passages recording what was once believed
(:60, :77) should KEEP their content and gain a dated supersession tag — the way TEST-PLAN:8
marks its own retired set — because erasing the record destroys the evidence that a correction
happened. Passages asserting present state or prescribing future work (:36, :102, :124, :329,
:336, :344) are simply wrong and should be corrected.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: DESIGN.md is the spec drive-status names for this repo, so an agent
reading it for what to build next finds a prescription for work that was deliberately abandoned,
and a description of CI weaker than the gate that actually runs. DESIGN.md already marks other
superseded items inline (the /sign contract at step 1 carries "[SUPERSEDED by ADR-0013 §2]"), so
the convention exists and these sites simply never got it.

This is an instance of btc-policy-0ip (normative rules duplicated across documents with no
per-rule authority).

VERIFY — a SWEEP, not a checklist, because every enumeration of this drift has been incomplete:
  (a) Read docs/DESIGN.md end to end against docs/TEST-PLAN.md:48's table, SCENARIO_NAMES, and
      .github/workflows/ci.yml. Every mention of attack scenarios, the harness, the demos, or CI
      either describes what ships today or carries a dated supersession tag.
  (b) No DESIGN.md passage schedules as "later"/"v1"/"Next Steps" anything that already exists
      and runs in CI.
  (c) grep DESIGN.md for the retired names -> every hit that USES THE NAME AS AN
      `attack --scenario` IDENTIFIER sits under a supersession tag. SCOPE THIS CAREFULLY; two of
      the nine are live vocabulary and must NOT be tagged:
        - `recovery-drill` is a CURRENT shipped command (`btc-vault demo recovery-drill`,
          main.rs) and a gated launch-gate step. Only its use as an attack-scenario name is retired.
        - hold/clawback is act two of `demo theft-refused` (the attacker's allowlisted spend

          as an attack-scenario name is retired.
      A blanket grep would force valid current references under a supersession tag, which is a
      worse defect than the one this bead fixes.
  (d) DESIGN.md's CI description matches ci.yml's actual jobs, legs and triggers.
Each checked separately; passing one says nothing about the others.

title: Recover exact clock-refused Carrier receipts through serialized outer-Stale classification
description:
Integration owner for btc-policy-sxt's receipt-recovery behavior. Blocked by completed btc-policy-5io and btc-policy-qzo, and has two sequential rb-lite code children; this parent adds no Rust beyond integration corrections proven necessary by child review.

## Children
- `btc-policy-7ip`: ordinary fresh-envelope new-holder authority, non-destructive clock refusals and 30-second retry classes. Hard cap **550 gross Rust = ~130 production + 420 tests**. Depends on 5io.
- `btc-policy-30c`: authenticated/quota-admitted outer-Stale receiver discrimination with `sign_state → store` acceptance-gap serialization and out-of-lock KDF revalidation. Hard cap **700 = ~150 production + 550 tests**. Depends on 7ip and qzo.

## Integrated contract
A new holder requires attempt `< E` and monotonic `< D`; fresh duplicate/completed confirmation is idempotent. One second is only for short InFlight/KDF-busy states; long actionable clock refusal is 30 seconds. Terminal/nonmatching outer stale remains terminal. q6v identity/alternate-signature/PIN-verifier bounds remain. Global high-water is unchanged and btc-policy-r1g owns its duration-unbounded outage.

## Closure evidence
Both children must capture red-first and named mutations, pass focused suites, and jointly prove all three refusal sites, acceptance→claim race, terminal outer-Stale matrix, quota/no-nonce behavior, KDF outside locks with revalidation, and pin-uniform bytes/work/state. Parent closes only after child reviews and the parent sxt integration/gates.

## Aggregate budget
**1,250 gross Rust maximum, all tests included: ~280 production + 970 tests.** Children own these lines. Parent evidence/docs cap: 48 rendered lines.

title: Replace outer-stale scheduler polling with deterministic test synchronization
description:
FOUND during PR #18 CodeRabbit/Opus/Tau review. The new `eventually()` helper polls at most 10,000 `yield_now` iterations. In the negative KDF-order test, worker starvation can make `assert!(!reserved)` pass before the worker reaches the guarded region; in the positive diagnostic test, starvation can produce a false red. The checked-in rb-lite review observed four `DIAG-NEVER-PUBLISHED` failures in 149 unmodified full-suite runs. The reversed KDF/sign-state mutation did reach the intended assertion and EXIT=101, so the property is not wholly unpinned. P3 test confidence/CI reliability, no production behavior.

## Scope
Replace both polling uses with deterministic test-only synchronization at the real milestone: before waiting on `sign_state`/attempting KDF reservation for the negative ordering proof, and after diagnostic publication while the worker is still blocked for the positive proof. A larger loop count or wall timeout alone is insufficient because it cannot make the negative assertion non-vacuous. Do not alter production scheduling, lock order, freshness behavior or budgets.

## Evidence
Observe the current helper's vacuity with a deliberately withheld worker milestone and its false-red shape under delayed publication. Green tests must have explicit witness channels/barriers and stay deterministic under repeated execution. Re-run the existing KDF-order and diagnostic mutations; each must still EXIT=101, with exact gate green.

title: Reproducible build pipeline: byte-identical rebuilds, signed artifacts, dependency gates in CI
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-gbw 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review). gbw had no blockers, so it could be closed against a commit lacking the stage-1 code; the freeze now waits for that code while THIS bead -- the pipeline that makes a freeze possible -- can start immediately.

DELIVER: (a) a REPRODUCIBLE BUILD -- pinned toolchain, deterministic flags, documented procedure -- such that an independent rebuild of a given commit yields byte-identical binaries. Verified by someone rebuilding on a DIFFERENT MACHINE; a hash produced by the same box proves nothing. Name who or what that second machine is (CI runner, a second developer box) rather than leaving it to the implementer. (b) SIGNED RELEASE ARTIFACTS -- state which key signs, who holds it, and how a verifier obtains the public half; a signature nobody can check is decoration. (c) cargo audit / cargo deny WIRED INTO CI, the gap docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md already admits and threat-model R4 records; this is independently landable today and should not wait for (a).

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ADDRESS (see btc-policy-4y3 and ADR-0012): reproducible builds are SUPPLY-CHAIN PROVENANCE. They close the poisoned-build and tampered-dependency vectors of residual R8b. They do NOT address malware resident on a correctly-built, correctly-verified running coordinator -- that needs no modified binary -- and they do not touch a wrench beginning mid-spend. The one narrow extra benefit is detection: re-hashing an installed binary catches malware that persisted by patching it, and only if the check runs from OUTSIDE the compromised host.

VERIFY: two different machines produce identical hashes for the same commit; CI fails on a known-vulnerable dependency (demonstrate with a deliberately pinned bad version, then revert); a third party can verify a release signature from published instructions alone.

title: Operator CLI slice: 'pending' — poll every node and diff against what the user authorized
description:
SPLIT OUT OF btc-policy-mby 2026-07-30 (codex+Fable bead review). Slice 3 of 4. DEPENDS ON the mby core substrate. Small, read-only, and independently landable.

WHY: docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md tells a user to poll /pending -- 'presumably by hand', as threat-model R9 records. This is the incident surface btc-policy-k0t built on the node side, with nothing on the operator side to consume it. THREAT-MODEL A7 answers the coordinator-auth-key thief by citing 'every node's pin-uniform GET /pending projection', which is only an answer if some tool actually polls it.

DELIVER: 'pending' -- poll GET /pending on ALL n nodes (not a quorum, and never via the coordinator's own view), present the accepted-candidate set per node, and DIFF IT against the spends this operator authorized.

THE HARD PART, which must be decided in this bead rather than left to the implementer: WHERE THE AUTHORIZED-COMMITMENT RECORD LIVES. Diffing requires durable local state recording what the user authorized -- but ADR-0010 makes the coordinator an untrusted relay, so a journal that lives only there can be edited by the component the diff is meant to catch. Specify the journal's location, format and trust properties, and state plainly what an attacker who controls the coordinator host can do to it. If the honest answer is 'nothing protects it there', say so and put it elsewhere.

ALSO: a divergence between nodes is itself the signal (one node holding a candidate the others do not is the arm-split shape ADR-0012 cares about), so present per-node disagreement rather than merging into one list.

VERIFY: a candidate accepted by all n shows as agreed; a candidate injected at one node only shows as divergent; a spend the user never authorized shows as unrecognized; the command works against a node set where one node is unreachable, without hanging or silently dropping it from the comparison.

title: Passive receipt clock destroys a ruled carrier memo and intent: raw-clock prune loses holder confirmations irrecoverably
description:
FOUND 2026-08-03 during btc-policy-9zs implementation (rb-lite round-9 panel, codex gpt-5.6-sol,
rated P0 confidence 10/10). PRE-EXISTING: verified byte-identical on origin/main before 9zs. Filed
at P1 rather than P0 because the trigger is an ENVIRONMENTAL clock fault rather than anything a
post-wrench coordinator controls -- but the consequence class is theft, not censorship, so disagree
with that downgrade if you have reason to.

## The defect

`ChannelState::carrier_memo_lookup` calls `store.prune_intents(now)` where `now` is the RAW wall
clock: production `handle_channel_body_now` passes `channel::unix_now` as `confirmation_clock`.
`prune_intents` retains both `intents` and `carriers_by_nonce` on `expiry > now`. A transient
forward clock excursion -- NTP step, VM restore, RTC fault -- past a live carrier's expiry therefore
DELETES this node's own arm intent and its `Derived` memo, on an untrusted read, driven by a
PASSIVE peer receipt rather than by anything this node decided.

This violates a rule the repo states explicitly in `NonceLog::effective_now`'s doc (replay.rs):
'Carrier intents must use this same value: pruning or confirming them against raw wall time after
the nonce log has advanced would let a clock rollback revive logically-expired confirmation state.'

## Why it does not recover

`NonceLog` deliberately does NOT advance `high_water` for a REJECTED forward-clock request
(replay.rs), precisely so one excursion cannot latch a bogus future mark and refuse honestly-timed
requests afterwards. That correct decision means nothing restores the deleted state once the clock
corrects. A later peer receipt resolves to `Vacant` -> `carrier = None` -> `ChannelReply::Accepted`;
`retry_loop` RETURNS on `Accepted`, so the sender never retries; `confirm_carrier` then finds no
intent and returns NONE forever.

## The stake

Section 0 arming counts receipts to reach t-of-n. A silently lost receipt can leave one honest node
UNARMED. Codex's chain: during the explicitly supported normal-to-duress resubmission, that unarmed
node plus t-1 compromised nodes can release and finalize the pending hot spend, because the freeze
is LOCAL. That is the unfrozen-quorum / theft class -- the same class `MemoOutcome::InFlight` was
added to close, arriving through a different door.

## What btc-policy-9zs did and did not do

9zs added `owner_still_ruling` so `prune_intents` retains BOTH an `InFlight` claim AND a `Derived`
memo whose owner is still ruling. That closes the half 9zs itself created. The remaining hole is a
RULED `Derived` memo whose intent has aged out -- the case the code comment calls 'the ordinary
expiry case'. So 9zs NARROWED this defect and documented the boundary in code; it did not close it.
Do not read the surviving asymmetry as an oversight.

## The decision this bead must make -- do not skip it

Making passive expiry non-destructive requires deciding what BOUNDS the two maps if untrusted reads
can never evict. `prune_intents_after_nonce_accept` is the authorized evictor today and is what
keeps them bounded. Options, each with a different bound argument:
  (a) route every passive prune through `effective_now` instead of raw wall time;
  (b) make passive prune fully non-destructive and rely solely on the accept-path evictor;
  (c) give memos a separate rollback-guarded horizon.
Pick one and STATE the bound argument. Do NOT fix this by widening `owner_ruling` to all `Derived`
memos without one -- that is precisely what makes the maps unbounded.

## Verify

A test that steps the receipt clock forward past a LIVE RULED carrier's expiry, lands a peer
receipt, steps the clock back, and asserts the intent and memo both survive and the receipt is
still counted. The existing `a_forward_receipt_clock_cannot_make_an_in_flight_claim_vacant_before_rollback`
(added by 9zs) is the template; extend it to the ruled case. Both maps must be shown to stay
bounded under the chosen option.
notes: Superseded intermediate-tree evidence (the named test existed at b6124d1 but was later consolidated), observed locally on 2026-08-12: after restoring the old passive `store.prune_intents(now)` behavior inside `carrier_memo_lookup`, `nix develop -c cargo test --locked -p vault-node --lib channel::duress::a_forward_receipt_clock_cannot_prune_a_ruled_carrier_before_rollback -- --exact --nocapture` exited 101 at the intended assertion, with map counts `(0, 0)` instead of `(1, 1)`. After restoring the fix, the targeted `channel::duress` suite exited 0 with 126 passed, and the authoritative AGENTS.md fmt/clippy/workspace-test gate exited 0. Separate mutations that removed generation binding and made a terminal non-staging refusal retryable each exited 101 in their intended focused regression. Full logs remain local execution artifacts; these outcomes record the required observed red/green rather than a static prediction. Final terminal-retry refinement evidence on 2026-08-13: after restoring the pre-refinement expired-Derived predicate, the module-qualified unruled-intent regression exited 101 with both the already-held and already-committed terminal checks false; restored code made the focused test and the exact authoritative AGENTS.md gate exit 0. The final Rust diff is 430 gross lines against origin/main (tests included), at the 430 hard cap after consistency corrections. title: Rollout stage 5: sealed hosts on mainnet (gated on the nju lifecycle decision)
description:
Rollout ladder stage 5 (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md): five machines, one provider, SEALED hosts, MAINNET. Full two-vault Path suite.

GATED ON btc-policy-nju BEING DECIDED — with stage-4 attrition data in hand. That ordering is the whole point of the 2026-07-29 decision: seal on signet first (stage 4, bead s12), measure how long five sealed nodes actually survive untouched and what a migration-to-patch really costs, and only then choose between immutable one-shot nodes and recoverable hardware-backed nodes with a durable monotonic Lockdown latch. Putting mainnet funds behind the wrong model is exactly what this rung waits for.

HONEST FRAMING (plan review, Fable Q5): this is a DEFAULT, not a pure deferral. Stage 4 cannot run without a sealed node image, and the seal IS the immutable one-shot model — so everything from stage 4 onward is built on model (a) unless attrition proves it intolerable. Also, part of the answer is knowable now: commodity cloud providers reboot and live-migrate VMs on their own schedule, and under ADR-0007 every such event is a dead node, so stage-4 attrition will likely be dominated by provider maintenance. Measure the magnitude, not the direction.

IF nju RESOLVES TO (b), hardware-backed with supported restart, a durable Lockdown latch is necessary but NOT sufficient — see the durable-state bead; and the external review's scope must reopen to cover the reworked core invariant, because the STAGE-1 FREEZE (btc-policy-gbw) froze a core in which reboot-death was load-bearing. Note this is now the freeze doing that work, not a review: ADR-0017 removed external review #1 entirely, so there is no stage-1 review that ever examined this core.

title: Coalesce repeated freshness diagnostics without evicting watchtower evidence
description:
Child of btc-policy-sxt. Implement only freshness-diagnostic coalescing needed so clock-retry traffic cannot churn unrelated watchtower evidence. It may land before the deadline substrate; depends only on closed q6v. The outer-Stale child btc-policy-30c depends on its final API.
