title: Forward channel-freshness high-water outlives clock correction and blackholes peer traffic
description:
FOUND during btc-policy-sxt SPEC review. The `/channel` ingress guard advances `high_water = max(high_water, raw_now)` before freshness classification and never lowers it. If the receiver wall clock jumps forward by Δ > the 300-second past tolerance and is then corrected, every honestly timestamped channel envelope—including `partial` and holder receipts—remains `STALE_TIMESTAMP` until real time catches the latch to within 300 seconds.

sxt deliberately keeps this global freshness invariant and gives only exact resident Carrier receipts a non-destructive fixed 30-second retry while sender expiry and the acceptance-fixed monotonic deadline remain live. That prevents immediate state loss but cannot make progress when `Δ - 300` outlasts either bound. There is no protocol bound on outage duration because Δ is not bounded. What remains bounded is resident state and the loss consequence: in the composite `t-1` compromised-nodes + stolen-Hot-keys case, failure to suppress an earlier pending Hot spend has the existing Hot-budget-bounded conditional-theft consequence; otherwise the path is denial/Recovery.

## Deliver

After sxt lands, re-evaluate the channel freshness authority without weakening envelope replay protection. Establish the smallest rule that lets genuine corrected-clock traffic make progress while preserving recipient binding, per-peer quota, nonce replay, PIN uniformity, and partial/receipt idempotency. Consider bounded high-water decay or an exact authenticated message exception only after proving its replay and state-oracle consequences.

## Non-goals

- Do not widen sxt or block its monotonic Carrier-retention fix.
- No general NTP service, persistence, or protocol/schema change without a separate reviewed decision.
- Do not claim a finite Lockdown acquisition bound; btc-policy-1y2 remains separate.

## Acceptance

- RED: latch receiver high-water forward by more than 300 seconds, correct raw time, and show fresh authenticated `request` and `partial` envelopes remain stale for `Δ - 300`; vary Δ to prove there is no protocol duration bound.
- GREEN: corrected traffic makes progress within a stated finite bound without accepting a captured/replayed envelope, bypassing quota, consuming a nonce on refusal, or creating PIN-dependent observables.
- Preserve sxt's exact Carrier stopwatch/retirement rules and run custody-critical gates.

title: V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest demonstration
description:
## V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness demonstrating the duress mechanism on a live n=2t-1 federation. Split from V0-4b-core per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across implementations. UPDATED 2026-07-20 to the mechanism the dual-model review settled: the signer/partial COUPLING + RELEASE-GATE is the theft proof (not the t-holder receipt count, which is timing), and the one residual (duress-signal censorship of a pre-pending normal hot spend from a sub-quorum) is BOUNDED by the V0-11 Hot budget (ADR-0014). Scenarios: toxic-parent, in-flight-refresh, two-spend-probe(silence), escape+refresh, arm-split-closed(coupling), censorship-residual-bounded(hot budget), partition, reboot-death, coverage/feerate fire-failure, recovery.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file .rb-lite/tasks/v0-4b-harness-adversarial.md is gitignored):

# V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness for the duress mechanism

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisite merged:** V0-4b-core (the two-track duress state machine) + the
  V0-11 hot-spend bound — plus everything they consume (V0-8b, V0-4a, V0-10).
  This bead is the **launch-gate adversarial demonstration**, split from the core
  per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across
  implementations: the core owns the production state machine + its unit/model
  tests; this owns the broad, environment-heavy regtest/CLI scenarios.
- Authoritative for the MECHANISM (read before writing a single assertion):
  - `docs/adr/0012-...` — the two-track state machine, the transition table, and
    the invariant list. **Two passages are load-bearing and were re-settled by the
    2026-07-20 dual-model (codex + Fable) review; the harness must assert the
    property they state, not the earlier one:**
    - the **"CORRECTION (2026-07-20)"** paragraph at the end of the §"Duress state
      machine" intro, and
    - the **"Partial-release authorization (both candidates)"** invariant (the
      release-gate).
  - `docs/adr/0014-hot-spend-bound.md` — the Hot budget (per-tx cap + velocity
    ledger) that BOUNDS the one residual this design leaves open.
  - `docs/DESIGN.md` (Success Criteria; attack scenarios), `CONTEXT.md`
    ("Duress PIN", "Hot budget").

## The mechanism this harness demonstrates (assert THIS, not the count)
The safety property is **not** "t nodes armed." With `n = 2t−1` and up to `t−1`
compromised, a holder set of size `t` has only `≥ 1` honest member, so a receipt
count can never *prove* `t` honest nodes froze — a receipt proves relay, not
freeze. The confirmation count is a **timing/liveness** mechanism (when the
freeze/sweep commit), not the theft proof.

What makes a coerced spend un-completable is the **signer/partial coupling +
release-gate** (ADR-0012 "Partial-release authorization" + the signing-oracle
prohibition):
1. **Coupling.** A node emits a partial for a candidate ONLY after independently
   receiving and processing that candidate's own user-authorized carrier (no
   peer message is ever a signing oracle). Processing a **duress**-pin carrier
   arms → freezes that candidate under the same store lock that would release it.
   So the set of honest nodes that hold a *releasable* partial for a
   duress-carried spend is a subset of the set that *froze* it — you cannot have
   an honest node that signed the carrier but did not freeze it. The arm cannot
   be split away from the signature.
2. **Release-gate.** Neither the spend's nor the escape's partial leaves the node
   before that candidate's authorized fire event; arming atomically + monotonically
   suppresses every existing and future hot-partial release. A hot candidate is
   never observable open-but-unfrozen (the freeze is set under the release lock).
3. **Result.** No honest node ever releases a coerced partial → only `≤ t−1`
   compromised nodes can → never a signing quorum. The sweep may still fail
   (funds sit frozen → recovery); that is denial, never theft.

**The one residual, and its bound.** A DIFFERENT case is not closed by the
coupling: a hot spend submitted EARLIER with the *normal* pin (legitimately
pending in Hold, every node holding an unfrozen partial), where a later duress
signal is **censored by a compromised coordinator** from a sub-quorum of honest
nodes — those nodes never freeze it and release at Hold-expiry. This censorship
residual is the accepted "hot wallet is the risk budget" residual, and it is
**bounded** by the V0-11 Hot budget (per-tx cap + rolling-window velocity), so
the most it can admit per window is one Hot budget, never the vault (ADR-0014).

## Outcome
An adversarial regtest harness (a `vault-cli attack`/`demo` subcommand and/or an
integration-test module) that DEMONSTRATES, end-to-end on a live regtest
federation (`n = 2t−1`, e.g. 3-of-5), that the duress mechanism holds its safety +
silence properties under adversarial conditions: freeze + lockdown → recovery, no
theft path, silent to an outside attacker, and the censorship residual empirically
bounded to the Hot budget. This is the empirical counterpart to V0-4b-core's unit
tests — the "wrench-attack answer is live" evidence.

## Why this exists
ADR-0012 says several duress properties are best "verified empirically … with an
adversarial regtest harness" — they involve process kills, network partitions,
mempool packages, and timing probes that unit tests can't fully exercise. And the
2026-07-20 review turned on a mechanism (coupling + release-gate vs. a receipt
count) that a live demonstration must pin down: the harness proves the *coupling*
holds against a coordinator that actively tries to split the arm from the
signature, and that the residual it does not close is bounded by the Hot budget.

## Required — the harness scenarios (each asserts the SAFETY outcome + no theft)
1. **toxic-parent**: an escape built over an external unconfirmed deposit →
   excluded (build-over-mempool); the escape either fires over vault-authorized
   inputs only or the sweep fails → Lockdown → recovery. No poisoned escape.
2. **in-flight-refresh**: a refresh in flight when duress arms → the escape
   chains off the refresh output (vault-authorized) OR the sweep fails → denial,
   never theft; the coerced hot spend is dead (frozen partial + unconditional
   Lockdown at T).
3. **two-spend-probe (silence)**: an attacker probing with two spends cannot read
   the duress bit — identical observable outcomes (latency, `/events`, peer
   traffic, response size) under both pins. Include the Hot-budget refusal path:
   a `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` refusal is pin-independent, so it does not leak the bit.
4. **escape-class + refresh sequences**: the two-slot record + `Idle→Armed`
   suppression behave per the transition table; escape-class completes + residual
   sweep over disjoint/union inputs; the normal pin's delayed slot is a no-op.
5. **arm-split-closed (the coupling — codex P0, 2026-07-19)**: a coerced hot spend
   submitted WITH the duress pin; a compromised coordinator tries to split the arm
   from the signature by making the carrier reach exactly ONE honest node and not
   the rest, via each concrete vector ADR-0012 names: (a) corrupt the user-signed
   escape so a peer's local policy refuses before propagation, (b) oversize the
   carrier past a peer's `max_msg_bytes`, (c) set an expiry that lapses mid-fan-out.
   **Assert the coupling, not a count:** the honest nodes that did not receive the
   carrier never signed its partial (no signing oracle), and the one(s) that did
   receive it froze it (release-gate). So at Hold-expiry the releasable partials
   number `≤ t−1` (compromised only) → the combine cannot reach a quorum → the
   coerced spend never broadcasts. Lockdown at T on the armed node(s) → recovery.
   There is no honest node that signed the carrier but left its partial unfrozen.
6. **censorship-residual-bounded (the Hot budget — ADR-0014 / V0-11)**: the case
   the coupling does NOT close — a hot spend pending under the *normal* pin, with a
   later duress signal censored from a sub-quorum. Demonstrate the BOUND, three
   parts: (a) an over-`hot_max_per_tx` coerced hot spend is refused at ingress at
   EVERY node with `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` **before signing**, so it never becomes a
   censor-completable pending candidate — and the duress arm still fires +
   propagates on that refusal path (composition); (b) within-cap hot spends whose
   window sum exceeds `hot_max_per_window` hit `HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED` at ingress on
   the 2nd+ (an attacker cannot queue several large hot spends in one Hold and clear
   them all); (c) the release path gives budget back — a hot spend cancelled/expired
   **while still unexposed** frees its reservation, while a broadcast/released one
   meters to age-out (monotonic window). Net: the censored-completion is bounded to
   ≤ one window's Hot budget, never the vault.
7. **partition / selective delivery**: deliver the duress carrier to a subset of
   nodes. Safety does **not** depend on every node arming; it depends on the
   coupling — assert no honest node releases a coerced partial regardless of how
   many armed. Drop the reachable-armed set below `t` → lockdown-only (no sweep, no
   theft) → recovery. (Contrast with the OLD framing "propagation arms every
   reachable node": that all-or-nothing arming is the timing story, not the safety.)
8. **process-kill / reboot-death**: kill an armed node (destroy its tmpfs
   deployment) before T → surviving armed set (≥ t) still fires the sweep; drop
   below t → lockdown-only; the killed node holds no keys/schedule/partials and
   cannot restart/rejoin (RAMDISK reboot-death). Also cover the lockdown latch
   surviving a PROCESS restart but dying on machine reboot (V0-4a durability).
9. **coverage/feerate/package fire-time failures** on live regtest → the sweep
   does not fire, Lockdown at T still happens (unconditional), funds recoverable
   via V0-10.
10. **recovery demonstration**: after a lockdown-only outcome, exercise the V0-10
    timelocked recovery spend (time-warp past the relative lock) → funds move via
    recovery. This makes "freeze + lockdown → recovery" a demonstrated exit.

## Tests / acceptance
- Each scenario runs on a co-located regtest federation (`n = 2t−1`) and asserts:
  no theft path (funds only ever reach vault/hot/escape/recovery, never an attacker
  address the user didn't author), the SAFETY track held (freeze + unconditional
  Lockdown at T), and — for the probe/timing scenarios — silence (indistinguishable
  observables under both pins, including the Hot-budget refusal path).
- The arm-split scenario asserts the **coupling** specifically: enumerate the
  honest nodes that emitted a partial for the coerced carrier and show every one of
  them also froze it (releasable-partial count ≤ t−1). A test that only counts
  "how many armed" is asserting the wrong property — it must show no signed-but-
  unfrozen honest partial exists.
- The Hot-budget scenario asserts the numeric bound: over-cap refused pre-signing
  at every node; window sum capped; released/expired reservations returned.
- A scorecard-style exit (like `demo first-light`) communicates pass/fail per
  scenario; the whole harness exits 0 when all safety assertions hold.
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` still exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-cli/` (attack/demo subcommand) + integration test modules;
  MINIMAL `crates/vault-node/` changes only if a test seam is genuinely needed
  (prefer driving the real daemon). Do NOT change the duress state machine
  (V0-4b-core), the channel, the release-gate, policy, or the Hot budget ledger —
  DRIVE them adversarially. If a scenario cannot be demonstrated without changing
  production safety code, STOP and flag it rather than weakening the mechanism to
  make a test pass.
- Non-goals: multi-VPS attack range (Approach B, later), the full v1 nine-scenario
  playbook — build the ADR-0012 denial-residual set + the coupling (arm-split) +
  the Hot-budget bound + reboot-death + recovery demonstration. No new production
  safety mechanism; no durable ledger (RAMDISK only). Size budget: a bounded
  harness over the existing daemon, not a re-implementation of the federation.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- The harness demonstrates, on live regtest (`n = 2t−1`), freeze+lockdown→recovery
  with no theft path and silence to an outside attacker across: the ADR-0012 denial
  residuals; the **coupling** (a coordinator that actively splits the carrier from
  the signature still cannot assemble a coerced quorum); the **Hot-budget bound**
  (the censorship residual capped to one window's budget, refused pre-signing);
  reboot-death; and recovery. The wrench-attack answer is empirically demonstrated,
  and it demonstrates the mechanism the 2026-07-20 review settled — the release-gate
  + coupling — not the receipt count.

title: Vault migration and rotation tooling: the routine response to a patch, a dead node, or a key change
description:
FILED 2026-07-30 from the codex+Fable bead review (BOTH reviewers). Two beads CONSUME a migration flow that no bead BUILDS.

THE GAP: btc-policy-s12 must time 'one migration-to-patch performed for real' and hits a wall at its own VERIFY. btc-policy-nju drills 'migrate a vault end-to-end'. ADR-0005 makes migration the ROUTINE patch procedure -- sealed nodes have no upgrade-in-place, so patching a node means rotating the vault. docs/UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY.md states outright that no tooling exists. DESIGN.md sketches the rotate flow (escape-class sweep to the escape wallet, then fund a successor vault at leisure) and stops there.

DELIVER: (a) create and verify a SUCCESSOR VAULT -- a fresh setup ceremony whose output is checked against the predecessor's parameters, so a migration cannot silently weaken the vault (a shorter timelock, a smaller federation, a reused key); (b) MOVE THE FUNDS by the correct permitted path -- an escape-class sweep through the normal path, never a recovery-branch spend, and never a path that requires the duress subsystem; (c) RETIRE the predecessor: mark deposit addresses dead, record which secrets are now burned, and make reuse of the old descriptor detectable; (d) KEY MATERIAL RULES -- ADR-0015 item 2b requires FRESH material at stage 6 because everything provisioned under the waiver sat inside one provider's console reach, so the tooling must be able to assert 'no key in the successor appeared in the predecessor'; (e) an AUDITABLE RECORD of what moved, when, and from which vault to which.

CONSTRAINT: migration is the response to a COMPROMISE SIGNAL as well as to a patch, so it must work when the predecessor federation is degraded -- some nodes dead, one node suspected. State the minimum live-node count the flow needs and what happens below it.

VERIFY: a full migration on regtest from a 5-node vault to a fresh one, with a deliberately dead node in the predecessor; the successor-verification step REFUSES a successor with a shorter timelock or a reused key; the audit record is sufficient to reconstruct what happened without the operator's memory.

title: attack escape-class-sequences fails locally, PASSES in CI (18/18) — the '16/16 cannot pass' framing is falsified; mechanism still undecided
description:
FILED 2026-07-31 while draining btc-policy-6nq. The adversarial harness reports 15/16, and MANY beads list 'attack 16/16' as an acceptance gate (6nq, 6nv, and the full-matrix requirement in gbw and 9y5.8). That gate cannot currently be met on main, so every bead carrying it is either unclosable or will be closed against a weakened bar.

ESTABLISHED BY TEST, not inferred:
- FAILS on feat/6nq-confirmed-escape-invalidation.
- FAILS identically on origin/main (eb916ff) -- so it is NOT caused by the 6nq change.
- FAILS identically at a1814c6, which predates the btc-policy-9y5.7 escape RBF fee-bump ladder -- so the ladder is not the cause either. It is older than that.
- Reproduces deterministically: three consecutive runs, three different txids, the same failure and the same ~190s runtime. Not intermittent within a run.
- The other 15 scenarios PASS, including every duress, reorg, lockdown and recovery assertion.

THE FAILURE: 'transaction <txid> never reached the mempool or a block' -- the generic settlement-wait helper at crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs:2058 giving up on a transaction.

HYPOTHESIS, NOT YET CONFIRMED -- test before believing it: this scenario is unusually timing-sensitive and machine-speed-dependent. escape_class_sequences (attack.rs:4900) calls calibrate_pin_cost() and then runs 16 Argon2-heavy samples, and its own comments say 'at the calibration ceiling the 16 Argon2-heavy samples below can take tens of seconds; T must not land mid-loop'. It uses hold_secs 120 / duress_delay_secs 90. The box these runs happened on is SHARED, MULTI-TENANT and was under sustained heavy load (a 6-hour rb-lite run plus review agents). A calibration that adapts to a loaded machine, combined with a fixed settlement window, is a plausible mechanism -- but 'plausible' is where this stops. It could equally be a real defect in escape-class settlement.

INVESTIGATE IN THIS ORDER: (1) re-run on an IDLE box and see whether it passes -- that single result decides between 'harness fragility' and 'real bug', and everything else depends on it; (2) if it passes idle, the bug is the scenario's timing assumptions, and the fix is to make the settlement window derive from the measured calibration rather than from a constant; (3) if it fails idle, this is an escape-class settlement defect on the CROWN-JEWEL fire path and the priority goes up, not down; (4) bisect properly to find where it broke -- it is older than a1814c6 and nobody appears to have noticed, which is its own finding about how often the full suite actually gets run.

DO NOT 'fix' this by loosening the assertion or marking the scenario ignored. A gate that many beads cite, quietly weakened, is worse than a gate that visibly fails.

VERIFY: the scenario passes 3 consecutive runs on an otherwise idle machine; if the fix is to the harness, it must be derived from measurement rather than a bigger constant; the root cause is recorded in the bead so the next person does not repeat this bisect.

DIAGNOSED 2026-07-31 (codex + Fable, both independently, same read-verified mechanism). HYPOTHESIS (A) CONFIRMED -- THIS IS NOT A SETTLEMENT DEFECT.

DECISIVE EVIDENCE: this scenario PASSED in 286s during rb-lite round 7 on this same box, on the code now merged -- 16/16 scenarios held (/tmp/rb-6nq-run/gate-attack-all-round7.log:111, calibration chose one Argon2 = 199ms at 28131 KiB). A deterministic settlement-logic defect cannot pass. It is load-sensitive.

THE MECHANISM, read-verified at line numbers by both reviewers: an escape-class spend fires IMMEDIATELY -- FireWindow { fire_at: now, deadline: min(expiry, now + combine_slack_secs) } (lib.rs:5337-5343, 5433-5438) -- and this scenario uses the minimum combine_slack_secs of 20s (attack.rs:386). Inside those 20 seconds the ENTIRE pipeline must complete: carrier fan-out to holder quorum, each honest node performing 3 memory-hard Argon2 evaluations AT THE CALIBRATED COST (up to 128 MiB), partial exchange, combine, package check, and broadcast -- with release, finalize and broadcast each re-checking the window at send time (channel.rs:4170-4173, 4325-4327, 4394-4401). Missing it is PERMANENT: the candidate can never broadcast afterwards, so the 45s wait_for_tx cannot recover it. A HOT spend does not have this exposure -- quorum forms during its 120s Hold and only the light release/combine/broadcast must fit the 20s window. escape_class_sequences is the ONLY scenario combining immediate-fire + single-node ingress (attack.rs:4987) + calibrated pin cost.

EVERY LEGITIMATE-REFUSAL MECHANISM WAS ELIMINATED by reading each gate: fire-time coverage and the panic-feerate floor apply only to the ARMED sweep (is_armed_escape requires armed.active && sweep_active, both false under the normal pin); the package is a singleton over confirmed inputs; no coin conflict exists among A/B/C/D before the duress T; per-peer quota is 600/min and not overridden; fee is ~85 sat/vB against a 1 sat/vB floor; coverage is 99.17% normal / 99.995% duress against a 95% precondition. 'Broadcast but unobserved' is also excluded -- wait_for_tx polls mempool AND chain every 250ms.

WHICH TRANSACTION: reasoned, NOT observed (both reviewers agree, both flag it as inference): the immediate NORMAL-pin escape-class spend of coin A, at attack.rs:5022. codex correctly notes the wiretap control at attack.rs:895 aliases to a similar ~190s and cannot be excluded from the artifact alone, because the error message is generic.

MY EARLIER BISECT WAS INVALID AND IS WITHDRAWN. I reported this as 'failing identically at eb916ff and a1814c6, so it predates the 9y5.7 RBF ladder'. That reasoning does not hold: every one of those runs happened on a box under sustained heavy load (a 6-hour rb-lite run plus concurrent review agents). I was measuring the load, not the commit. There is no evidence this is old, and the round-7 pass is evidence it is not.

THE FIX (neither reviewer would accept a raised constant, and neither should this bead):
(1) DERIVE combine_slack_secs from the calibration rather than pinning the 20s minimum. It is already a per-scenario Setup field (attack.rs:350, 389). Scale duress_delay_secs with it, since control_separation_secs and the no-op-control margins consume it. The scenario ALREADY owns this pattern -- its sampling-window guard (attack.rs:5147-5163) derives a budget from measurement and fails loudly -- it just never applied it to the immediate legs. Note its headroom comment guards the WRONG risk: it worries about T landing mid-loop while the unguarded budget is [ingress, ingress+combine_slack].
(2) ADD THE MISSING GUARD: refuse at the top, the way 5154 already does, when the measured per-carrier pipeline cost does not comfortably fit combine_slack_secs -- turning a silent wait_for_tx death into an attributed calibration error.
(3) NAME EACH WAIT. The generic 'transaction X never reached the mempool or a block' is a real diagnostic defect: it made the failing transaction unattributable and is why the answer above is inference. At minimum: 'wiretap control', 'normal A', 'duress B', 'duress residual'.
(4) codex's alternative, worth considering: split into a fixture-cost four-coin sequence proving A/B settlement and the no-op/residual semantics, plus a calibrated silence probe for body/size/latency uniformity. The 16 expensive samples are not needed to establish the four-coin chain semantics.

SAME-CLASS EXPOSURE: two_spend_probe is the only other calibrate_pin_cost caller (attack.rs:3957) and shares the fixed 120/90s windows -- same fragility class, currently passing. hold_expiry_race's WRENCH_LEAD_SECS = 4 is machine-timing-sensitive in the same spirit.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: see btc-policy-9yf. There was no watcher — no CI run reported a result anyone acted on. (The original wording here, "CI has never run, 44/44 failures at job startup", is RETRACTED as of 2026-08-09. .github/workflows/ci.yml OWNS this history and carries the re-measurement — about half those runs executed for the full gate duration and failed rather than dying at startup. Read the figures there; they are deliberately not repeated here. Do not re-cite 44/44 or "never ran" from here.)

STILL TRUE, AND STILL THE POINT: under either hypothesis the scenario's actual claim -- that an escape-class spend is pin-uniform, verified on-chain because the acknowledgement cannot distinguish the two -- does not get verified on a loaded machine, because the run dies at a precondition. Fixing the window is what makes the silence assertion reachable.

UPDATE 2026-08-01 — CONFIRMED PASSING ON CI, and the fragility class is broader than this bead.
escape-class-sequences PASSED on CI run 30666082498 at 272s, independently confirming the load-sensitivity diagnosis on hardware that is not this box. But on run 30683094069 it FAILED again with a DIFFERENT failure — a timing-oracle assertion at 317.6ms skew, where run 1 measured 2.27ms on identical code. So this scenario has now failed two distinct ways for two distinct reasons: settlement-window starvation under load (this bead) and noise-dominated timing measurement (bead btc-policy-c9r). Fixing the combine window will not make it green; both need fixing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
STEP (1) IS ANSWERED, 2026-08-12, by evidence gathered incidentally while draining
btc-policy-nia. This bead's own instruction was: "re-run on an IDLE box and see whether it passes
-- that single result decides between 'harness fragility' and 'real bug'."

THE TITLE OF THIS BEAD IS FALSIFIED and has been retitled. "The 'attack 16/16' gate cannot
currently pass" is false: it passes routinely.

MEASURED:
  CI, dedicated GitHub runner, branch fix/nia-harness-negative-control:
    18 successful workflow runs, each containing a launch-gate job whose `attack all` step
    reported 16/16 -- 47 to 51 minutes per run. This is the closest available thing to the idle
    box step (1) asks for, and it is not close: it is green every time.

  Local, on the SAME shared multi-tenant box this bead blames, but not under a 6-hour rb-lite load:
    escape-class-sequences PASS 284s   (during nia's Escape-fault attack-all run)
    escape-class-sequences PASS 282s   (during nia's Hot-fault attack-all run)
  Both runs went 16/16 overall. A third run shows FAIL 412s, but that one is not evidence for this
  bead: nia had deliberately disabled Lockdown at T, which broke 15 of 16 scenarios including this
  one. Do not count it.

RETRACTED 2026-08-12, same day, after codex review. An earlier version of this section argued that
because the failures ran ~190s and the passes ran 282-284s, "loaded box => slower => misses a fixed
settlement window" could not be the mechanism -- and concluded the remaining work was step (2)
rather than step (3). THAT INFERENCE IS INVALID and is withdrawn.

Total runtimes are not comparable between a pass and a fail here. A FAILING run returns EARLY at
`wait_for_tx`; a PASSING run then continues through the later sleeps, the sampling loop, mining, the
no-op window and the duress-T checks (crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs:5232-5568). So a run can miss
the ~20s ingress-to-broadcast window and still post a much SHORTER total, purely by skipping the
rest of the scenario. The comparison measures how far each run got, not how fast it ran.

To actually discriminate, compare THE CRITICAL WINDOW -- the ingress-to-broadcast interval -- not
wall-clock totals. That measurement has not been taken.

CONSEQUENCE: step (2) vs step (3) is NOT settled. The loaded-runner/fixed-window model is still
live, and so is the possibility of a real escape-class settlement defect on the fire path, which
per step (3) would RAISE the priority. Do not read the CI evidence above as closing that question:
it shows the gate passes routinely on a dedicated runner, which is worth knowing and falsifies this
bead's original title, but says nothing about which mechanism causes the local failures.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the fragility is not fixed, and the scenario can still fail under
load, so beads citing "attack 16/16" as a gate should still expect an occasional red locally. It
also does not explain the original failure's mechanism -- only that it is not "the gate cannot
pass". And nothing here was run on a genuinely idle dedicated box outside CI.

STILL BINDING from the original filing: do NOT 'fix' this by loosening the assertion or marking the
scenario ignored.
notes:

FURTHER, ON THE LOADED SHARED BOX ITSELF: during the btc-policy-9zs rb-lite run (2026-08-03,
9 rounds over 15h) `attack all` completed 16/16 with escape-class-sequences PASSING on at least

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: the root cause is still the timing coupling this bead diagnosed --

inside which the whole carrier fan-out, three calibrated Argon2 evaluations per honest node, partial

DO NOT close this as 'works now'. The correct close is either the measurement-derived window, or an

title: Rollout stage 4: sealed hosts on signet — MEASURE node attrition
description:
Rollout ladder STAGE 4 ONLY (docs/ROLLOUT-PLAN.md). Stage 5 is btc-policy-qbt; this bead was split on 2026-07-29 so the nju decision could depend on stage-4 data instead of preceding it. Five machines, ONE provider, hosts SEALED per ADR-0005 in full (no SSH, no administrative path, no upgrade-in-place, reboot kills the node), SIGNET. Runs the full two-vault Path suite.

Operates under ADR-0015's test-only waiver of ADR-0009: one provider is a correlation class holding quorum, and sealing does NOT fix that — ADR-0005 concedes a VPS is never fully sealed against its provider (console and rescue access remain).

THE POINT OF THIS STAGE IS MEASUREMENT, not just hardening. Sealing makes patching a node cost a whole vault rotation and gives a dead node no remedy. Whether that is livable is an EMPIRICAL question, and stage 4 answers it cheaply — signet funds. Record: how long five sealed nodes actually survive untouched; what killed them; and the true wall-clock and ceremony cost of one migration-to-patch performed for real, not estimated.

Part of the answer is predictable and should not be presented as an open question: commodity cloud providers reboot and live-migrate VMs on their own schedule, and under ADR-0007 every such event is a dead node. Expect attrition to be dominated by provider maintenance. Measure the MAGNITUDE, not the direction.

THIS STAGE'S DATA DECIDES btc-policy-nju (immutable one-shot nodes vs recoverable hardware-backed nodes with a durable monotonic Lockdown latch). The graph reflects that: s12 BLOCKS nju, and nju blocks qbt (stage 5, mainnet). Do not resolve nju before this stage produces numbers.

DEPENDS ON btc-policy-nwd (the ADR-0005 sealed NODE image — note this is NOT btc-policy-4y3, which is coordinator-host hardening, a different machine and a different threat), btc-policy-azn (on a sealed host /healthz is the ONLY observability, so a node silently pinned to full scans is exactly the health signal this stage must see), and stages 2-3 (btc-policy-4wx).

VERIFY: full Path suite on both vaults; an attrition record with real durations and causes; one migration-to-patch actually performed and timed; the data handed to nju in a form that can decide it.

title: Preinstall and attest the operator CLI in the sealed runtime image
description:
FOUND by the 2026-08-18 post-recording Opus audit of the mby split. M6 intentionally proves only the rollout-stage-1 artifact-to-command path on an open regtest host. It does not prove that the operator CLI binary is present and invocable on the later ADR-0005 sealed runtime host.

The v0 node API is loopback-only, so live commands must execute on the co-located host. ADR-0005 forbids general administration/install-after-seal; omitting the CLI from the image at ceremony time is irreversible for that vault and reproduces the pre-mby “sealed but cannot operate” failure despite correct command code.

## Scope
- Give the operator CLI an explicit owner in the reproducible release/image pipeline before rollout stage 4.
- Package and preinstall the reviewed `btc-vault` binary and only its declared runtime dependencies before sealing; bind/record its binary hash/version with the build/release evidence owned by btc-policy-oy3.
- Prove the sealed image can invoke the production operator command against local loopback nodes/Core without a post-seal package manager, shell update or network install path.
- Define replacement behavior honestly: changing the CLI after seal requires the existing reimage/rotation lifecycle, not an in-place exception to ADR-0005.
- Keep secrets external to the image; no user key, coordinator-auth secret or PIN is embedded in the binary/package.

## Non-goals
Implementing operator commands (mby), changing loopback transport (imb), opening an administration plane, general node-host packaging, or weakening sealed-host invariants.

## Evidence
A stage-4 image built without the CLI must fail a pre-funding readiness check. The complete image must report the expected reviewed binary hash, run the production artifact loader/command against local services, and expose no package-install/update mechanism after seal. Mutation omitting/replacing the binary must turn the stage-4 readiness gate red.
close_reason: REJECTED 2026-08-18 (PR #20 review): this bead conflated the dedicated coordinator host with an ADR-0005 sealed node host. vault-cli is the coordinator and belongs on btc-policy-4y3's hardened coordinator build, with btc-policy-oy3 owning reproducible signed artifact identity. ADR-0005 exposes no interactive invocation/secret path; installing spend/escape there would be unusable without violating that boundary and would co-locate the user key, PIN and coordinator credential with a node signer. Stage 2+ uses btc-policy-imb's confidential authenticated coordinator ingress, so stage 4 does not retain the v0 loopback premise. The s12 dependency is removed. If this task had remained, nwd ordering would have been necessary but insufficient. Operator artifact installation/hash/invocation readiness is now explicit in 4y3/4wx, not a new node-image task.

title: Seal network in manifest revision 2 and refuse the wrong Core chain
description:
CHILD A OF btc-policy-5ag — sealed network byte, manifest schema revision 2, backend identity, address plumbing, independent Core evidence, and neutral artifact path. This is an explicitly NON-DEPLOYABLE intermediate. It authorizes no production ceremony; child B must close before the parent or rollout stage 1 can close.

PROBLEM / THREAT MODEL.
- A node currently accepts any Core backend satisfying IBD/txindex/relay-fee checks; `getblockchaininfo` is already fetched at `crates/vault-node/src/chain.rs:675`, but its chain identity is ignored. Against another chain the vault UTXO view, confirmation state, Escape coverage, and broadcasts are wrong. Empty/wrong coverage can leave no admissible Escape and force the 180-day Recovery path precisely during duress.
- `chain:"signet"` is a chain type, not sufficient identity. Default and custom signets share it. The same Core response carries `signet_challenge`; code 2 below means the default/global public signet used by the spend recorded in `docs/SIGNET-SPEND-RECORD.md`, while this child's Core oracle owns the exact challenge's provenance.
- Network does not alter BIP32 derivation or descriptor scriptPubKeys. It selects xpub/tpub and address encodings and identifies the backend chain. Do not regenerate/migrate keys or introduce per-network policy.

DELIVER — SMALLEST DESIGN.
1. Use `bitcoin::Network` in policy/runtime state. Raw string exists only at the config deserialization seam and is parsed once. Allowed ceremony/config spellings are exactly `bitcoin`, `signet`, `regtest`; testnet, testnet4, aliases, and garbage fail with the allowed set. Keep `PolicyParams: Copy` via a small custom serde adapter; do not enable bitcoin's serde feature; no serde default.
2. Add a canonical manifest `network:u8` after `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` and before node count. Explicit mapping: Bitcoin=0x01, public Signet=0x02, Regtest=0x03. Never use `Network as u8`, enum order, or a string in the preimage. `Testnet4` was inserted into rust-bitcoin's enum and demonstrates why ordinals are unsafe.
3. Atomically change `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 1→2. `/v0` domain tags stay unchanged. Revision 1 and 0 configs fail with the version diagnostic before missing current fields, wrong anchors, descriptor errors, or network I/O. There is no legacy decoder/preimage.
4. Thread the single value through ceremony input/state, manifest JSON, the one node-config writer and every fixture/emitter, `ConfigFile`, `Node`, `ChannelState::build`, and backend startup. A network changed in one node config must change its manifest hash and fail against the sealed anchor; the failure names network.
5. Extend `verify_required_indexes(&self, sealed_network)` using the `getblockchaininfo` response it already fetches; no new RPC/startup phase and `main.rs` ordering stays load→validate→bind. Before IBD: require a string `chain`, parse Core's name, require exact sealed network, and refuse unknown/absent/non-string/testnet/testnet4. If Signet, require the exact default-public `signet_challenge` constant (case-insensitive valid hex after trim); absent/empty/null/custom refuses and names public-vs-custom. For non-Signet, a present non-empty challenge refuses as contradictory; null/empty is absent. Only after identity passes may IBD/txindex/relay checks run.
6. The public signet challenge constant lives beside the backend check, not in the manifest. It defines what sealed code 2 means and is pinned from a live offline default-signet Core response. Custom signet is unsupported and would need a new sealed identity/revision. Record residuals: two independent regtest instances and a forked backend that truthfully retains `chain:"main"` are not distinguished; no periodic recheck is added.
7. Thread `NodeParams.network` through the SEVEN ceremony-backed address sites only: demo.rs:323/431, signet.rs:203/279, attack.rs:545/667/4694. `recovery.rs:98` and `attack.rs:1272` remain explicit Regtest with a comment because neither consumes a ceremony/sealed artifact. `Wallet::random` receives the expected network kind so harness descriptors are flavour-consistent. Avoid a network framework or per-network policy object.
8. Rename `SEALED_DIR` from `sealed-v1` to neutral `sealed`; revision identity belongs in manifest JSON. Update setup docs and the LIVE target clauses in btc-policy-b8z and btc-policy-finalize-staging-reclamation-sq7 atomically with the code. Preserve genuinely historical M1 wording and do not rewrite `.beads/.br_history` archival snapshots.
9. A still leaves the descriptor-kind relation unenforced. Ensure every A vector/fixture is flavour-consistent from birth: mainnet rows hand-write xpub-flavoured hot/Escape descriptors; signet/regtest use tpub. `keygen --role escape` still emits Test-kind until B, so during A it prints a loud runtime warning naming the mismatch and B. Docs state A is non-deployable and B owns the gate. B must not re-freeze A's three protocol digests.
10. Update `CONTEXT.md` with the domain term Vault network; `PROTOCOL-VECTORS.md`, ADR-0013, SETUP-CEREMONY, THREAT-MODEL, ROLLOUT-PLAN, UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY, OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK and inline manifest docs must agree. The runbook's startup-refusal table names wrong chain and wrong/custom public signet plus the remedy. No new ADR.

INDEPENDENT ADDRESS/CHAIN EVIDENCE.
Parameterize the private ignored Core harness in `crates/vault-node/tests/bitcoind_backend.rs` for main/default-signet/regtest: isolated datadirs/RPC ports, correct cookie subdirectory, `-connect=0`, `-listen=0`; existing backend tests retain Regtest behavior. Before changing the renderer, make Core reproduce a current frozen descriptor/address. Then for one fixed vault descriptor, use Core `getdescriptorinfo` + `deriveaddresses` offline/unsynced on all three networks, compare with fixed in-tree constants and the real production renderer, and freeze the results in a non-ignored test. The ignored leg also reads the public signet challenge from Core. It proves descriptor→script/address encoding against independent C++, not operator intent, real-chain behavior, or that any particular wallet rejects tpub.

RED-FIRST / MUTATION PROOF (real failed assertion + intended diagnostic; restore checksums after each mutation).
A1. Update frozen manifest/endorsement/envelope expectations to revision 2 + the network byte before implementation; observe red. Recompute all three outside Rust only after that method reproduces all revision-1 digests. Mutations: omit byte; reorder it before the ceiling (same length/multiset); feed a constant code. Include at least two network values so the constant-code mutation cannot survive.
A2. Ceremony JSON with `network` is an unknown-field red on the base tree. Green table accepts the 3 values, rejects testnet/testnet4/garbage, and proves the gate is on real assemble/config output.
A3. Extend preflight rows: revision 1/0/absent outrank missing network, mismatched network, wrong anchor, descriptor errors. Use one live recording RPC sentinel for BOTH legs: old revision records zero requests; same reachable server with a current config records at least getblockchaininfo. An empty/dead server is invalid evidence. Mutating preflight past backend I/O must kill the negative leg; the record must say whether a bypassed old config loaded/hit I/O.
A4. Backend identity table covers 3 matches, 6 cross-pairs, test/testnet4, absent/non-string/unknown chain, absent/empty/null/custom signet challenge, unexpected nonempty challenge on non-signet, and identity/challenge + IBD=true with only getblockchaininfo scripted. Identity diagnostics outrank IBD and no later RPC occurs. Mutations independently drop chain comparison, accept unknown, accept custom challenge, alter the public constant, or move identity after IBD. The load-bearing challenge mutation that drops only the comparison must kill the custom-challenge row and no unrelated row; the value mutation must set the public constant to the custom fixture and be killed by the live default-signet challenge provenance row.
A5. Federation/config disagreement changes manifest hash and fails startup. A constant network passed into the manifest must be killed. Cross-revision endorsement uses previous revision 1. Current missing field names network; current different value names sealed-anchor mismatch.
A6. Core oracle is non-tautological: expected values are checked-in constants; a mutation replacing expected with Core's own output must be rejected as invalid evidence. Default signet reports the exact pinned challenge; a custom challenge differs/refuses.
A7. Source/behavior audit proves exactly the seven ceremony-backed address sites consume `NodeParams.network` and the two named private-Regtest sites remain explicit. A hardcoded-Regtest mutation must kill signet/mainnet renderer rows.
A8. Publication tests literally expect `sealed/`, retain owner-only/atomic behavior, and docs plus the live b8z and sq7 target clauses use the neutral term; archival history remains untouched.

HARD BUDGET (tests INCLUDED).
- Rust: 1,150 gross additions+deletions against A's claim base, including every production line, test, helper, fixture and generated assertion. Estimate 352 production + 593 tests = 945; cap includes >=20% contingency and reserves approximately 425 production / 725 tests (63% tests).
- Non-Rust: 230 gross additions+deletions, non-transferable to/from Rust. Estimate base 177: PROTOCOL-VECTORS 60; SETUP-CEREMONY including L3 disclosure/rename 62; ADR-0013 20; UPGRADE/ROLLOUT/THREAT/RUNBOOK/CONTEXT and inline docs 25; live b8z/sq7 bead plus DRIVE wording 10. Arithmetic is 177 + 36 (>=20% contingency) + 17 (review-round allowance) = 230.
- At 950 Rust, inventory all remaining obligations. If the full backend identity/challenge table OR all three protocol vectors is unwritten, STOP AND RESHAPE before further implementation. The pre-identified technical line is schema/rev2/preflight/sentinel/config/artifacts/vectors/neutral path versus backend identity/public challenge/Core oracle/address plumbing/vectors, but no new child is authorized until its >=20%-contingency caps, edge transformations, status/landing order and B dependency are reviewed and recorded. Do not compress proof to fit.
- At 200 non-Rust with either the L3 disclosure or protocol-vector truthful limits unwritten, STOP AND RESHAPE rather than omit them. Any cap breach is stop-and-report.

NON-GOALS.
No descriptor NetworkKind enforcement/keygen network flag (B); no custom signet/testnet/testnet4; no genesis RPC; no network serde feature/newtype; no per-tick backend recheck; no per-network policy; no multi-chain demo harness; no `/v0` tag change; no production authorization.

Manifest revision 2 seals Bitcoin/default-public-Signet/Regtest as explicit codes 1/2/3; old revisions preflight before current schema/hash/I/O; startup binds to Core chain identity and exact public-Signet challenge before IBD; all seven ceremony-backed address sites follow the sealed network; live artifacts use neutral sealed/; all three fixed protocol digests and offline Core address oracles are pinned. Exact hard-budget range 312d983ac07d239ea4a20097b260049890c97bc0..ce1025dc2b0b186ace22b8421613d7f016bcda2a: 1,150/1,150 gross Rust including tests and 187/230 total non-Rust. The 187 total includes six gross .beads/issues.jsonl bookkeeping lines; code/docs excluding those Beads lines are 181 gross non-Rust. Assertion-level red and mutation proof covered omit/reorder/constant network byte, chain/challenge/order, non-vacuous preflight-I/O, address plumbing, publication, artifact emission, descriptor precedence and non-tautological Core oracle. Final Codex current-head rounds were clean; Opus found no unadjudicated P0-P2; temporary-warning automation dissent was independently adjudicated P3 because real CLI/manual evidence exists, A is non-deployable, and child x00 replaces the seam. title: Prove setup assemble emits the sealed ladder disclosure
description:

However, the test invokes only that pure formatter. Deleting the sole production `assemble_cmd` print would leave the test green, so the operator-visible ceremony output is not mutation-bound. This is P3 evidence/maintainability: current production bytes are correctly wired and reviewed, but red-first item 4 of M1 asked to capture setup disclosure.

Add the smallest deterministic output seam or process-level capture that exercises the real `setup assemble` command path. It must prove the emitted operator ceremony includes: the sealed zero ceiling, fixed 180-day recovery timelock, replacement-rungs-only scope, base Escape excluded, concrete base fee unavailable at seal time, and exactly two transactions at zero. A mutation deleting/bypassing the production output write must make the test red. title: Escape fee ladder derivation: compose and user-sign the rungs the sealed escape_bump_max_fee_pct admits
description:
FOLLOW-ON to btc-policy-mby, split out during the 2026-08-05 owner grilling. mby seals the POLICY
(the `escape_bump_max_fee_pct` manifest field, its Ceremony input, and the validation; btc-policy-wdu owns the combined timelock/ladder prompt); this bead
builds the BEHAVIOUR that consumes it. Decisions and rationale: docs/adr/0016.

## What exists already

`escape_fee_ladder` (crates/vault-cli/src/fed.rs) ALREADY composes the ladder for the demo path:
rungs at ESCAPE_BUMP_MULTIPLIERS = [4, 16, 64] x base fee, funded from the LARGEST escape output
(not the last -- a Fable 9y5.7 review finding), dropping any rung that exceeds
ESCAPE_BUMP_MAX_FEE_PCT of swept value, would leave a sub-dust output (ESCAPE_BUMP_MIN_OUTPUT_SAT =
10_000), or fails to clear the node's incremental-relay minimum. The node accepts an empty ladder
(`if bumps.is_empty() { return Ok(()); }`). It does NOT refuse a ladder on an escape-class spend:
the only ladder gates are the length cap (lib.rs:5495), `ensure_escape_ladder` -- whose
`self_paired` flag is COMMITMENT-ID EQUALITY, not class -- and per-bump `verify_escape`. A valid
escape-class request (distinct disjoint residual, per lib.rs:5849) carrying a ladder passes all
three. So "an escape-class spend produces no ladder" is a CLIENT-SIDE CONVENTION this bead may
adopt, not a node-enforced rule; if it is adopted, say so and do not assert the node enforces it.

So this is mostly WIRING, not design. The work is making the operator CLI use it against a SEALED
vault rather than an in-process fixture.

## Deliver

(a) Replace the hardcoded ESCAPE_BUMP_MAX_FEE_PCT with the SEALED manifest value mby adds. At 0 the
    ladder is empty and the Operator approves exactly two transactions PER SpendRequest (a
    RefreshRequest presents one) -- that path must stay first
    class, not an edge case.
(b) Use the operator CLI signing seam contract owned by mby: hand off the spend, mandatory Escape,
    and composed `escape_bumps` together for user authorization. mby defines and implements the
    seam; this bead only populates the rungs through it.
(c) Derive replacement-rung fees from the base Escape composed by mby. mby owns the production
    feerate source and must produce a base admissible against the sealed `escape_feerate_floor`;
    this bead consumes that base fee and applies the fixed multipliers and drop rules. Do not choose
    a second, independent feerate source for the rungs.
(d) Surface what was composed before the user signs: how many rungs, at what fees, what share of the
    swept value the top rung pays. An Operator authorizing rungs they cannot see is the same
    unlabelled-PSBT problem the seam's shape was chosen to avoid.

## Verify

- A vault sealed at 0 produces, FOR A SpendRequest, an empty ladder and exactly TWO TRANSACTIONS
  PRESENTED for approval
  (not two signatures — a multi-input PSBT takes one per input, so signatures are not a stable
  observable; see ADR-0016). Assert the COUNT,
  not just that it works -- the two-transaction default is the decision this whole thread turned on.
- A vault sealed at a non-zero value, ON A FIXTURE CHOSEN TO ADMIT ONE, produces rungs whose top fee
  is within the sealed ceiling, and every rung is ACCEPTED by a live node at ingress (not merely
  composed). Do NOT assert that a non-zero ceiling always yields rungs: for a small swept value, a
  high base fee, or a large relay-size minimum, every 4x/16x/64x candidate can breach the ceiling,
  the dust floor, or the relay increment even at a generous percentage. A valid non-zero
  configuration that still yields an EMPTY ladder is a supported outcome and needs its own case.
- A ladder composed against a sealed ceiling near the node's own guard is REFUSED BY SETUP, not
  discovered at T. (mby owns that validation; this bead proves it holds end to end.)
- DECIDE, then test, whether a VALID escape-class spend may carry a ladder. A valid one has a
  DISTINCT DISJOINT residual Escape (lib.rs:5849), and that residual is a real delayed sweep that
  nodes will happily fee-bump. Be precise about WHAT would lose bumping: the clawback SPEND itself
  fires immediately and is registered with an empty `escape_bumps` regardless, so omitting the
  ladder costs it nothing. What loses bumping is the DISTINCT RESIDUAL Escape, whose fire window is
  the delayed one. So the real question is whether that residual needs rungs under duress -- decide
  that, rather than assuming the blanket rule is either safe or harmful. Only the SELF-PAIRED shape genuinely has nothing to bump, and that shape is refused outright
  anyway. Whatever is decided, assert on what the CLI composes -- the node enforces no such rule.


## Documentation consistency

Correct `docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md` §6's coercion procedure in this delivery. Only freeze plus
Lockdown-at-T are unconditional; the node merely ATTEMPTS the best-effort Escape sweep at T, and
coverage, the feerate floor, `testmempoolaccept`, or non-confirmation can leave the funds frozen for
Recovery. Step 2 must check which outcome occurred rather than presume the coins moved. This is a
wording correction to the existing two-track mechanism, not a new fallback or operator ceremony.

## Non-goals

Changing the multipliers, the funding-output choice, or the drop rules -- those were settled by
btc-policy-9y5.7 and its review. Changing the node-side rung SELECTION at T (ADR-0012 owns it).

title: Forward-clock paths retire confirmation-pending Carrier state and terminalize recoverable holder receipts
description:
FOUND 2026-08-12 while hardening btc-policy-q6v. q6v made passive carrier lookup non-destructive and proved a bound by letting later accepted nonces collect old carrier state. That bound is not safe against the remaining production clock authorities: the accepted transition still samples a wall clock that can be transiently forward, and several other paths destroy or terminalize holder evidence from bare clock observations.

## Defect

A transient forward wall-clock reading can still lose a live holder receipt through five production surfaces:

- the 1 Hz fire driver passes raw `unix_now()` through `prune_store` to intent/memo pruning;
- `/sign`, `/refresh`, and COMMIT-HOLD re-read `NonceLog::effective_now`, which prevents rollback but passes a forward excursion;
- `confirm_carrier` can cross expiry between lookup and its final clock sample, destructively remove state, then return terminal `Accepted`;
- outer `/channel` freshness permanently answers `STALE_TIMESTAMP`, and `retry_loop` treats every rejection as terminal, even for an exact receipt this node could count if real time catches the latched high-water before the signed deadline and retirement horizon;
- an unrelated accepted coordinator nonce can advance/prune from the same forward sample, so it is not independent expiry authority.

The result is an erased or permanently abandoned holder receipt. A confirmation-pending node may remain unarmed; the externally permitted outcome set remains ADR-0012's bounded residual (an already-pending, Hot-budget-bounded spend, an Escape, or no transaction before Recovery), but the current code reaches it from a transient local clock fault rather than the documented censorship boundary.

## Resolved design

### Carrier lifetime and identity

At the atomic coordinator-nonce acceptance transition for every channel-mode Spend request capable of owning a Carrier, capture accepted effective wall time `W`, process-monotonic instant `M` from that channel's production-fixed, test-pinnable `HotClock`, and signed expiry `E`. Admission requires `E > W`; checked arithmetic fixes the immutable retirement deadline `D = M + (E - W)`, which stays on the accepted Spend nonce entry until it lapses. There is no later pin-release transition or second clock source. Later wall-clock changes, retries, relays, Carrier retirement, and alternate signatures never move `D`. A wall clock already wrong at acceptance can make `D` too early or late; that admission-time fault is an explicit residual rather than a reason to trust later wall samples. PIN-symmetry state projections use a test-pinned `HotClock` distinct from wall `now` and include the deadline rather than masking it. A node built without channel mode has no Carrier/`HotClock`; its Spend nonce lifetime remains wall-only.

The authenticated request body is the Carrier identity; `coord_sig` is authentication, not identity. One resident Carrier owns one coordinator nonce. Exact retries and alternate valid signatures resolve to it. A different body cannot create an overlapping generation while that nonce's replay/fan-out tombstone remains.

### Clock refusal and receipt retry

Raw wall time, `NonceLog::effective_now`, fire/handler re-reads, later accepted requests, and confirmation resampling may refuse the current attempt but may not retire, replace, or extend an active or confirmation-pending Carrier. An at/past-signed-expiry attempt to add a new holder never adds a holder, opens a release gate, commits, or arms. A fresh duplicate/completed confirmation remains an idempotent no-op; outer-Stale already-held/completed remains terminal.

At the memo lookup, post-KDF lookup, and final-confirmation clock-refusal sites, an exact authenticated and quota-admitted receipt returns fixed `RateLimited { retry_after_secs: 30 }` while the acceptance-fixed monotonic deadline is live, the active/ruling or staged intent remains actionable, the decision is uncommitted, and the authenticated sender is not already counted. One-second retry remains reserved for short owner-in-flight and nonblocking-KDF-busy states. The attempt mutates no nonce, capacity, holder, gate, commit, arm, candidate, eviction, or lifetime state.

Outer `STALE_TIMESTAMP` has one receipt-only exception after peer authentication and quota charging: bounded zeroizing decode and full coordinator-signature/body verification precede identity lookup. Every stale envelope still calls the same freshness diagnostic and consumes no envelope nonce. Diagnostic publication keys on `(peer, ingress freshness high-water)`: lower concurrent observations drop; an equal high-water updates a retained entry in place without changing its sequence and does not resurrect an evicted entry; only a strictly higher high-water may append. A latched-high-water outage therefore publishes at most once per peer; if cap-evicted, equal-high-water retries do not republish it, preserving unrelated on-chain watchtower evidence. Final eligibility briefly serializes `sign_state → store` so it cannot observe the acceptance-to-Carrier-claim gap protected by q6v. An alternate-signature KDF claim is made there, the memory-hard work runs outside both locks, and its result is revalidated after reacquisition. An exact live actionable receipt returns the same fixed 30-second retry. Under the current premise `coord_nonces.high_water < E`, receiver clock correction can recover only after real time comes within the 300-second past window before `E` and `D`; retries end at those bounds, not forever. A larger excursion can blackhole authenticated channel traffic for unbounded real time; `E`, `D`, capacity, the Hot budget, and Recovery bound state/loss consequences, not outage duration. Already-held, committed, horizon-ended, malformed, unknown, non-Spend, wrong-expiry/body, invalid-inner-signature, and other nonmatching cases retain terminal `STALE_TIMESTAMP`. The exception never enters ordinary `/sign` ingress; the exact verified tag remains KDF-free.

### Alternate coordinator signatures

Strict DER and low-S do not make signatures from a hostile coordinator unique. Preserve q6v's verified-signature-tag fast path and bounded memory-hard equality check:

- verify every coordinator signature against the complete incoming canonical body before computing or using its tag;
- require exact resident nonce and expiry, live horizon, uncommitted decision, and an uncounted sender before Carrier KDF admission;
- exact original or already-resolved tags are KDF-free;
- one unseen alternate signature may make at most one nonblocking KDF attempt per sender and resident generation; busy leaves the allowance unused and is retryable;
- equality records only the safe verified-signature tag; mismatch spends that sender's allowance and remains terminal; a third unfamiliar signature cannot run another KDF, while the exact resolved signature remains usable;
- alternate resolution allocates no nonce or Carrier state and never restarts `D`;
- an expiry mismatch, already-held sender, or committed decision performs zero KDF work.

Never retain a fast digest, MAC, or full signature/body verifier for the PIN-bearing canonical request. A later process-memory capture would turn it into a cheap PIN oracle.

### Capacity and retirement authority

Reuse the existing `MAX_COORD_NONCES` coordinator-admission ceiling; add no Carrier-specific cap, lease, counter, config, manifest field, refusal code, or protocol version. Every accepted channel-mode Spend nonce records `D` and stays live while either wall expiry or `D` lives; non-channel Spend and Refresh remain wall-only. An active or confirmation-pending Carrier owns its matching memo; every settled `Derived` memo names exactly one intent, while a live `InFlight` memo may precede intent creation. An early or completed Carrier retirement may leave a nonce-only tombstone. All nonce types share that existing ceiling without double-counting.

At capacity, preserve every resident, consume no newcomer nonce, perform no PIN or Carrier-KDF work, evict nothing, and do not relay a request whose nonce was not consumed. This keeps the existing fan-out termination invariant. General `/sign` handler admission and mutex fairness remain btc-policy-1y2's responsibility.

Carrier intent and memo retire atomically under the existing store lock only on:

1. a genuinely non-staged terminal owner exit (including unwind/panic cleanup);
2. completion of the full pin-uniform normal-release or duress-freeze holder-decision transaction, not its intermediate `committed` marker;
3. `mono_now >= D` once no handler owns/rules the generation; or
4. reboot/process death.

The store-locked prune pass may execute (3) wherever it is driven—the 1 Hz fire tick, `/sign`, or `/refresh`—using `HotClock` monotonic time; the caller's raw/effective wall value has no Carrier-retirement authority. Owner-exit/unwind and holder-decision retirement remain store-only; no cross-lock pin release is introduced.

Candidate/fire-window expiry is a separate authority and remains unchanged. No raw/effective wall value, unrelated accepted request, capacity pressure, HTTP disconnect/timeout, staged refusal, receipt, replay, or alternate signature may authorize Carrier retirement.

The replay/fan-out tombstone in `NonceLog` is not deleted with Carrier state: immutable `D` lapses naturally, and ordinary nonce pruning removes the entry only after both signed wall expiry and `D` have ended. This supersedes only q6v's accepted-nonce Carrier-eviction/bound mechanism. It preserves q6v's non-destructive passive lookup, identity-unresolved `InFlight` retry, exact-tag fast path, bounded nonblocking re-signature work, busy-without-claim rule, no-fast-PIN-verifier rule, sender/generation binding, and terminal already-held/committed behavior.

## Non-goals

- No trusted clock/NTP service, persistence, wire/schema/protocol change, manifest/config field, or general wall-clock remediation.
- No general `/sign` HTTP admission, mutex fairness, or deadline-priority work; btc-policy-1y2 remains open.
- No global `/channel` freshness-high-water repair; the all-message outage after a larger forward excursion is tracked as btc-policy-r1g.
- No candidate, fire-window, Hot-budget, delivery-horizon, or Refresh-policy change.
- No new attack-harness scenario; deterministic state-machine/integration coverage owns this defect.
- Do not make an at/past-signed-expiry attempt add a new holder, commit, or arm; fresh duplicate/completed confirmation remains idempotent.

## Bounded implementation split

- `btc-policy-qzo` — freshness-diagnostic coalescing; hard cap **400 gross Rust = ~110 production + 290 tests**.
- `btc-policy-o5g` — channel-mode acceptance-fixed deadline and nonce liveness; hard cap **650 = ~230 + 420**.
- `btc-policy-0hv` — store-only Carrier retirement, after o5g; hard cap **950 = ~280 + 670**.
- `btc-policy-7ip` — ordinary receipt attempt authority and 30-second retry classes, after 5io; hard cap **550 = ~130 + 420**.
- `btc-policy-30c` — serialized outer-Stale classification, after 7ip and qzo; hard cap **700 = ~150 + 550**.

`btc-policy-5io` and `btc-policy-ok4` are integration owners for their two code children. All caps include additions and deletions and every test line. Total hard cap is **3,250 gross Rust lines: ~900 production + 2,350 tests**; tests are budgeted at 2.61× production from measured repository/q6v test density rather than hidden or compressed. `sxt` remains the closure owner. `r1g` remains blocked on completed `sxt`.

## RED acceptance evidence — observe on the pre-fix/q6v tree

1. Drive the real `fire_tick`/`prune_store` path past a staged Carrier's signed expiry, correct the wall clock, and show current code deleted intent+memo and the peer cannot recover its holder receipt.
2. Drive real `/sign`, `/refresh`, and COMMIT-HOLD post-acceptance rereads across another Carrier's expiry and show current destructive pruning (direct tests or a shared authority test plus explicit caller assertions).
3. Through `handle_channel_body_with_clocks`, lookup before expiry and confirm after it; show current `confirm_carrier` deletes state and returns terminal `Accepted` without counting the holder.
4. Latch `/channel` outer freshness forward by more than 300 seconds but less than the Carrier's remaining lifetime, then correct the raw wall clock; show an exact actionable receipt returns terminal `STALE_TIMESTAMP`, `retry_loop` stops, and the node cannot reach `t` even after test time advances back inside the latched 300-second window.
5. Show a live memo with the same nonce but different expiry consumes a guaranteed-useless Carrier KDF; show already-held and committed senders can likewise consume useless alternate-signature work.
6. Show current wall-expiry/supersession behavior can replace a nonce-keyed memo while older carrier-keyed intent state remains.
7. Fill the alert queue, repeatedly reject the same peer at one latched freshness high-water, and insert continuing unrelated watchtower alerts between rejects; show current remove+append publication repeatedly displaces additional unrelated evidence.
8. Capture each intended test red before the fix, per AGENTS.md.

## GREEN acceptance criteria

1. Channel-mode Spend acceptance fixes `D` once with checked arithmetic from the production-fixed, test-pinnable `HotClock` and stores it until it lapses; non-channel Spend/Refresh remain wall-only. Tests cover just before, exactly at, and after `D`; later raw/effective clock excursions, Carrier retirement, and alternate signatures neither move `D` nor retire state. A horizon landing while the owner is ruling cannot delete under it; the eventual owner exit resolves safely. PIN-symmetry shape tests pin `HotClock` to a value distinct from wall `now`, include the deadline, and correct the stale `SignStateShape` clock comment.
2. Every `prune_store` driver—fire tick, `/sign`, and `/refresh`—may execute exact-`D` store retirement, but it, COMMIT-HOLD, passive lookup, nonce pruning, and confirmation cannot retire Carrier state from a bare wall/effective sample. Candidate cleanup remains byte-for-byte semantically unchanged.
3. The three receipt clock-refusal sites and outer-Stale receipt-only exception return fixed 30-second retry only for an exact live actionable Carrier; one second remains limited to short `InFlight`/KDF-busy states. The crossed attempt adds no holder, commit, or arm. Under the current premise `coord_nonces.high_water < E`, after correction and enough elapsed time to re-enter the latched 300-second freshness window—while `E` and `D` live—a fresh envelope can count and the t-th receipt completes the full holder-decision transaction. Retries end at `E`/`D`; a larger excursion may make the channel unavailable for unbounded real time, while only retained state and loss consequences are bounded.
4. Table tests pin terminal outer-Stale cases: already-held, committed, horizon-ended, unknown, wrong expiry/body, invalid inner signature, malformed payload, Refresh, and partial remain `STALE_TIMESTAMP`. The final check takes `sign_state → store` and cannot miss q6v's acceptance-to-claim `InFlight` window. Every stale outcome calls the same freshness diagnostic, charges quota once, consumes no envelope nonce, and is PIN-uniform in bytes, work counters, and masked state. Lower/equal/higher ingress high-water tests cover concurrent ordering, same-sequence in-place update, no equal-high-water resurrection after eviction (and the documented diagnostic-absence consequence), higher-high-water append, cursor behavior, continuing unrelated alert flow, and queue cap.
5. Exact signature tags are KDF-free. One alternate valid signature—including through the outer-Stale receipt exception—receives at most one nonblocking KDF attempt per sender/resident generation; the KDF runs outside `sign_state` and `store`, then revalidates after reacquisition. Busy consumes no claim; equality records only the safe tag; mismatch/third signature is terminal. Expiry mismatch, already-held, and committed cases run zero KDFs. No path extends lifetime or capacity.
6. One resident Carrier per nonce: exact retry and alternate signature reuse it; the NonceLog replay/capacity predicates treat a monotonic-pinned but wall-expired entry as resident, so a different body cannot overlap it. Keep supersession/reinstallation defenses even when the protected path makes them unreachable; stale owner cleanup cannot touch a later post-retirement generation.
7. `MAX_COORD_NONCES` remains the sole admission ceiling. Replay/capacity predicates keep every accepted channel-mode Spend nonce resident while either signed wall expiry or `D` lives; non-channel Spend/Refresh stay wall-only. At full capacity a newcomer consumes/relays/derives/evicts nothing; capacity frees only when the applicable lifetime ends. Transition tests distinguish an active/confirmation-pending Carrier with matching memo, a settled `Derived` memo with exactly one intent, an active `InFlight` window, and a valid nonce-only tombstone after early/completed Carrier retirement; no global cardinality equality is claimed.
8. Every authorized Carrier remover/executor is covered: poison-tolerant non-staged owner exit/panic, fully completed normal and duress holder-decision transactions, every store-prune driver at exact monotonic horizon after owner release, and reboot model. Races retire intent+memo exactly once without touching immutable nonce `D` and never revive state.
9. Capture named mutation controls that independently break: wall-or-monotonic nonce liveness, exact-`D` boundary, 30-second long-lived retry, outer-Stale acceptance-to-claim serialization, post-KDF revalidation, and lower/equal/higher diagnostic-high-water behavior. Each intended test must first be red per AGENTS.md.
10. Capture green exit codes. Run the exact AGENTS.md gate, ignored regtest backend, and full launch gate (three demos plus `attack all`) because this is custody-critical.

title: README.md describes a project that no longer exists: single co-signer + CTV upgrade path, contradicting DESIGN/CONTEXT — and it is the public front page
description:
FOUND 2026-08-04 by the multi-reviewer-loop's cross-file consistency pass while reviewing
btc-policy-9zs. PRE-EXISTING and unrelated to that bead — README.md predates the 2026-07-13
redesign and was never edited. Filed rather than fixed inline because rewriting the project's
public self-description is an editorial decision, not a consistency touch-up.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ORDINARY DOC DRIFT: this repository was made PUBLIC on 2026-07-31.
README.md is the first thing a visitor reads, and it currently describes a different system than
the one in the tree.

THREE CONTRADICTIONS, each verified against the authoritative side:

1. ARCHITECTURE. README.md:3 says "an isolated policy co-signer" — singular. CONTEXT.md:3 says
   "a user hardware key plus a t-of-n federation of policy-enforcing signer nodes". docs/DESIGN.md:13-15
   names the single-co-signer shape ("IDEA.md's original 2-of-2 design — one host compromise away
   from useless") as THE FLAW the federation exists to fix. The README therefore advertises the
   design the project explicitly abandoned.

2. COVENANTS. README.md:3 promises "a future upgrade path to CTV/CCV covenant vaults".
   docs/DESIGN.md:259 says "**CTV/covenants are out of scope.** No covenant backend seam, no
   covenant-readiness requirement: this is a soft vault on today's consensus rules, full stop."
   These cannot both stand.

3. AUTHORITY. README.md:5 says "See IDEA.md for the full design document". CONTEXT.md:3 designates
   docs/DESIGN.md plus ADR-0012/0013 as the authoritative design documents. A new contributor
   following the README lands on the superseded document.

THE DESIGN/CONTEXT/ADR SIDE IS CORRECT in all three. The fix is to README.md.

DECIDE, do not just patch prose: what is IDEA.md for now? Options are (a) keep it as a historical
record and say so at its top, (b) delete it, or (c) fold anything still live into docs/DESIGN.md.
Leaving it unmarked while the README points at it as authoritative is what produced this.

VERIFY: README.md's opening paragraph describes the t-of-n federation, the user key, and the
timelocked recovery path; makes no covenant promise; and points at docs/DESIGN.md. Then grep the
repo for any other reference to "co-signer" (singular), "CTV", "CCV", or IDEA.md-as-authoritative
and confirm each remaining hit is either historical-and-marked or correct.

title: Duress incident procedure needs human security review, not another AI pass
description:
The duress incident procedure in docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md ("The user was coerced (duress PIN
used)") was rewritten SEVEN consecutive times during the ADR-0016 review loop (passes 26-33). Every
single round, the next review found a NEW defect in the freshly written text, several
safety-relevant. This bead exists because that pattern is the finding, not the individual defects.

WHAT THE ROUNDS FOUND, in order -- each introduced by the previous round's fix:
- assumed the sweep always lands, so the no-sweep branch abandoned a vault still holding the funds
- stated recovery maturity as one deadline when the BIP68 lock is per-UTXO and reset by refresh
- sent the operator to read `older(n)` from `manifest.json` (frozen constant; not a knob)
- then OVERCORRECTED to "it is NOT in manifest.json", which is also false (setup.rs:1621, 1633)
- deleted the "Once safe" coercion gate and replaced it with urgency wording, so the procedure told
  a possibly-still-captive victim to run a ceremony generating the new vault's keys and PINs
- serialized the new vault behind up to 180 days of straggler maturity, parking swept funds in a
  single-key escape wallet
- told the operator to verify Lockdown by SUBMITTING a spend or refresh -- which on a
  not-locked-down node can release a refresh and RESET the recovery timelock the procedure depends
  on two steps later
- claimed "nothing below is time-critical", false when the carrier never reached t: nothing armed,
  a coerced hot spend can still finalize, and hold_secs has no positive lower bound

All of the above are FIXED (commits 1c9c9b8..f2ab677 plus this one). What is NOT resolved:

1. THIS SECTION NEEDS A HUMAN SECURITY REVIEWER. Seven-plus AI rewrites each destabilized
   safety-critical incident text; several introduced NEW defects while fixing old ones (a deleted
   coercion gate, funds parked in a single-key wallet for months, a verification step that could
   reset the recovery timelock, and a Lockdown check forgeable by the very adversary the section is
   about). This is concrete evidence for btc-policy-9y5.8 deliverable (3) -- an external HUMAN
   review that this repo's own codex+Fable panels cannot satisfy. Do not close this bead with
   another AI pass.

2. DO NOT RESTATE ADR-0016 HERE. Earlier revisions of this bead listed the open ADR-0016 questions
   inline and went stale three separate times as those questions were decided -- twice telling a
   future implementer to do something the ADR had already established was impossible. The ADR is
   the authority: read docs/adr/0016-the-escape-fee-ladder-is-sealed-and-opt-in.md §3a and §4 for
   the current state of the preimage, protocol-version and ceremony-atomicity decisions, and
   btc-policy-mby for what ships. Nothing about them is a closing requirement for THIS bead beyond
   (a) below. (This is the duplicated-normative-content problem filed as btc-policy-0ip, in
   miniature, in a bead I created.)

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING, and it is not only reviewer noise: the runbook describes operations that
DO NOT EXIST. There is no sealed-vault receive, balance, or spend command, and no operational code
reads manifest.json (R9). Steps 3-6 are prose about a system one layer more finished than the one
built -- exactly what btc-policy-mby's WHY already records. Prose describing unimplemented
operations has no implementation to be checked against, which is why each careful rewrite produced
a new plausible-but-wrong instruction. A banner saying so was added at the head of the section, but
the real fix is mby + en1 landing, after which this procedure should be re-derived FROM the shipped
commands rather than polished further.

VERIFY: (a) MOVED TO btc-policy-yt7 by ADR-0017 -- a human security reviewer reading this section end to end, and (d) below's non-author dry run, are now part of the ONE external review at stage 9. They are DEFERRED, not deleted: the evidence for needing them is this bead's own history. This bead closes on its mechanical conditions; (b) the section agrees with whatever ADR-0016 says at review time -- checked then, not asserted here; (c) once mby and en1 land, every step names a
real command and the banner comes off; (d) MOVED TO btc-policy-yt7 (see (a)): a dry run -- someone who did not write it follows the
procedure on signet against a deliberately partial sweep and reports where they got stuck. This is the ONLY check anywhere in this repo that tests executability by someone without the author's context, which is why it was transferred rather than dropped.
